It's pretty much impossible to hate on a game like Marlow Briggs And The Mask Of Death. It is self-aware as can be, knowing it's a lot of nonsense. Marlow is armed with its crazy, ridiculous, and off-the-wall story: Marlow dies and is brought back to life to avenge his death, to save his girlfriend Eva, and stop a corrupt man from trying to rule the world. If that isn't enough - Marlow is constantly making a barrage of in-jokes aimed at video-games in general, action movies + games, and other things of that sort; and tons of non-stop action + explosions. And for most of this action/platforming game - what nonsense it is! Marlow is just tons of fun and will make you grin + smile, most of the time.
Most of the time, constanly running at 60 frames per second on my PC (i7 950; GF GTX 560 Ti; 8 GB RAM; Win 7 64-bit) - Marlow runs extremely well. Very rarely did it even drop below 60! Not only that - but the art-direction + technical graphics are surprisingly actually good here, as well. Marlow's non-stop barrage of action feels fantastic in the controls department with an XBox 360 Controller, playing and feeling very similar to the Darksiders series - which is fantastic! Combat feels + looks smooth, fast, and always is on point! If you're into action-games like the Darksiders (which many feel is similar to God Of War series, which I don't have and haven't played b/c I am a PC gamer) - you'll probably feel right at home with Marlow.
Just when you think you've had your fill of using a certain weapon or skill, expect more to suddenly come your way. Expect a suddeny upgrade to a skill or new game-mechanic introduced. And if this isn't enough - Marlow has mini-games of collecting objects in a race-like manner (which can be compared to on the Leaderboards); and even a mini-heliocopter game that feel like a throwback to Capcom's 1942 + Taito's Sky Shark. Marlow will constantly surprise the player with things like this, from in-jokes to game-references.
If this sounds up your alley, Marlow is sure to put a lot of cheesy smiles on the face of gamers. That is, until the last few levels come around, when the game decides to severely spike up in difficulty. Regardless, since most of your time spent for the 6-10 hours this campaign should last you (took me a bit longer than 10 hours b/c some areas were a bit frustrating to get though), Marlow is going to deliver a riotous, ridiculous, hilarious, and very fun action-packed roller-coaster ride of a game!
Final Grade = C+.

Porting performance issues and DRM turn this from a mediocre hack-and-slasher into a Do Not Buy. This is a $5 game and a pretty solid example of getting what you pay for.
The gameplay is decent, pretty good actually, but the story is slow and the platforming sections often feature really frustrating and stupid pixel-perfect jumps. Graphics are... decent.
The combat is pretty solid though, with a variety of weapons and spells. Unfortunately you might have a hard time executing your combos when your framerate suddenly drops into the single digits for no identifiable reason. On top of that, the controls are pretty... weird. with dual mapping between mouse buttons and i, o and p, for one example. This leads to some confusion when QTEs reference one set of these controls when you're using the other. On top of that, the game refuses to accept any controller that isn't an XBox 360 controller, so if you have a logitech gamepad or something else, sorry, but you're screwed. Lern2Joy2Key.
Overall, I would recommend this to someone who likes this kind of game, if not for the porting issues and DRM. The DRM is of the "♥♥♥♥ your progress the connection dropped so I'm kicking you back to main menu" variety. If you don't have a stable internet connection, I would strongly advise you stay far away from this game entirely.

How many times have you encountered a threequel that's better than both the original and the sequel combined? Well, you've already encountered one of them -- I'm reviewing it right now and you're reading it. Again, I don't think words can possibly describe WHY this game is amazing, so I'll just write a few of the little things I love about this game in no particular order.
1. Charging through every area in Risky's boots (this also functions as an anti-frustration feature if you want to buy something but you haven't a single gem to your name, as it's a very quick and easy way to get money and items)
2. RISKY REDEMPTION ARC. I repeat, RISKY. REDEMPTION. ARC!
3. The art (I especially love the new Rottytops)
4. Rottytops in general (and all the other characters -- everyone is more likeable in this game)
5. Pretty much all of Shantae's interactions with Risky from Saliva Island onwards are ADORABLE (especially arriving at each island, where there's always that moment Shantae forgets Risky used to be her nemesis)
6. If you don't get all the cacklebats before the final boss, you'll feel more horrible for it than when you unlocked the "heart of stone" and "play dead" achievements in Risky's Revenge. That's right, it has two endings. I can't imagine a better ending than the "true ending," though. Never in my life have I wanted to hug a pirate so much in either ending.
7. MELT! THEM!! DOWN!!!
8. "Men are idiots. At least I still have Wrench." -- Sky (this is also her card quote, by the way)
9. Shantae trying to be a pirate (I just really wish Risky was there to hear "moist the main snail")
10. THE MUSIC. SALIVA ISLAND. SPIDERWEB ISLAND. Just... ALL OF THE MUSIC.

First things first: Just like anchovies or hot sauce, THIS GAME IS NOT FOR EVERYONE.  TRY THE DEMO BEFORE YOU BUY.  The demo will give you a good feel of whether you will like the full game.
Even though I hit the "Yes, I would recommend," button—this is more of a mixed review. (I wish there was a middle option.)  Dead State requires deep thought and sometimes a touch of research.  There is more than one way to play—but you have to figure them out.  Although I personally liked going back to get my stats just right for my personal play style in the demo, not everyone will enjoy doing so.  This is not meant to be an easy game for those that want to just smash up some zombies for an adrenaline rush and gore fest. The game isn't something I'd recommend for the player that just wants to have some easy fun.  It is quite the opposite.
The game isn't very forgiving of mistakes and the right answer isn't simply handed to you.  Options are limited, negatives for the team are abundant and the player character is the only fully customizable ally.  You're forced to work with what you get, even the other survivors.  There is no “hone my skills to perfection by grinding first” easy button.  This game is meant to intrigue your mind and push your planning abilities.  For those hard core players that want to nitpick the details and get things just right, I'd say download the demo and dive in.  The save files even carry over from the demo.

Medieval engineers is the second game in the engineers series by Keen Software House, after Space Engineers.
This review will touch on several topics concerning this game.
Table of contents:
1. Developers
2. Gameplay
3. Look and feel
4. Content
5. Stability and bugs
6. Conclusion (TL;DR version)
1. Developers
I think it's very important to address this first, since at the time of writing there's some serious accusations being thrown about. This game is NOT abandoned. The company, keen, consistently updates this game weekly, and since a total work ethic change a few months ago, became one of the most consistent, structured ones i've seen.
Updates are weekly on a tuesday, alternating between content updates, like new things to build, and bugfixing/stabilizing/optimizing updates. Once every few months, a major update is released, like planet-sized maps or farming/ores. i can't say i've ever seem them miss an update by a lot, unless they had a very good reason for it.
2. Gameplay
Medieval Engineers plays like a mix between a survival and sandbox game. While the survival part has been traditionally rather barebones, improving on this has been the team's focus for quite some time now. Farming and tech progression are just some of the things the team has added to make this a richer experience over the course of the last year.
As for the sandbox part - Medieval engineers isn't story-bound and allows the player to create whatever they want - there's also a creative mode to omit the survival aspect entirely for those who purely want to focus on building magnificent structures from the get-go. Despite the presence of creative mode, survival isn't compromised, and everything you can build in creative can be built in survival.
3. Look and feel
Medieval engineers, just like space engineers, takes a mostly realisti approach in it's visual style. the game is quite detailed but as a result does put a bit more
4. Content
At this point, medieval engineers has a pretty decent ammount of content. there are still things both major and minor that are desired to be added, but there's definetely enough for a base game. While vanilla itself already allows one to richly decorate buildings from the inside and outside, both in terms of furniture and architectural variation, the modding community definetely helps by adding things that are too specific in taste for the game to automatically have for everyone. That is of course, not to say the mods fill the holes that the game leaves unfilled, it just adds those niche things that are more of an expansion than part of what would make the game whole.
5. Stability and bugs
I am aware that this section can be rather personal, and that's exactly why i beg your consideration when taking this in account while rating the game. the thing about bugs is that they're not always consistent. I personally haven't encountered any bugs that made me frustrated while playing. (honestly, i can't say i've encountered one recently at all), but i know that other players have. However, it's safe to say that at the moment there's no game-breaking bugs that are widespread across larger part of the community, or if there are, they are usually fixed in one or two updates. the dev team has dedicated every odd update entirely to fixing bugs and stabilizing and optimizing the game.
6. Conclusion (TL;DR version)
In my experience, medieval engineers is on the right track. It still has a way to go to reach it's full potential, but is definetely showing both promise and the will to move forwards. the game is pretty solid at this point, and it doesn't seem like the dev team is stopping anytime soon, with terraforming being the next major update set to release soon. While it definetely made a very slow start, it's picked up speed since 2015. i have to admit that i entirely quit playing somewhere in 2015 because the game was progressing so slowly, but when i came back to it a couple of months ago, i saw that it had grown into something far greater than what it was then. i think that given time, this can be a really solid game, and it's already pretty neat to play.

One thing I would like to see is a use for the lesser weapons. I found that once I researched a more expensive weapon you would always want to make only that one if you had the resources. Perhaps this could have been accomplished by having some buyers desire certain price ranges or something. I found a similar pattern with the shop upgrades where you just try to save enough to buy the most expensive stuff and that is always the obvious choice. I think an example of the old Diablo II is in order here. See in Diablo II the upgrade paths for the players had multiple but exclusive viable upgrade paths. So each character had a few different cool ways you could build them. If you chose one of those ways then you could not really try the other options. This made me want to play new games later where I could try the other character development options. So with upgrades to the the shop in potatoes it would have been cool if there were different ways you could go that were equally viable but different and exclusive to the other ways. It also would have been cool if there were lots of purely asthetic upgrades like all different color wallpapers and stuff to just give another thing to make me want to get money. The other thing that needs adjusting is the pacing of the game. To make a good weapon you need most of your crew all working so that means they can't be off selling or researching. Net profit from a full load of sales is rather small relative to what you need to buy materials. So progress ends up being rather slow and I find myself often waiting on a worker or two. So the pacing combined with too obvious upgrade system just turns it into a grind I think. It's all pretty hard to say for sure. Rating: 7.5/10
Overview: 3rd Person Action Adventure- Fun but unoriginal
The Good:
+ Surprisingly, for a game this age the graphics both artistically and technically are very good
+The combat system is fun, fast and fluid, and why wouldn't it be, it is a direct copy of the combat in God of War. You have light and heavy attacks creating different combinations, blocks to reflect enemy projectiles, dodging, and magic.
+4 different weapons and magic to fit your play style
+ Throughout the game you will visit interesting locations each providing its own unique action set pieces. The game does a good job of varying up the gameplay to a certain degree to keep things interesting.
+easy achievements
+The game is short but I consider that pretty good for this game because it doesn't wear out its welcome, it does everything it sets out to do.
The Bad:
- The game itself is very competently made, however its biggest "flaw" is that it is very unoriginal. God of War came out before this game and does just about everything better in every category. This is the biggest clone of God of War I have ever seen, from the combat to the platforming to the moves. This in itself isn't bad as many games copy each other however this game brings absolutely nothing new to the table. I know you should judge a game on its own merits but its highly obvious the developers looked at God of War and re-skinned it.
- The story is an afterthought and serves as an excuse for you to kill lots and lots of enemies. After the first 5 minutes of the game the entire story is laid out before you. It doesn't help that the dialogue is terrible.
- Every character in the game is generic, its hard to care about anyone in the game
- Outside of combat the platforming and controls can be a bit flaky at times.
Conclusion
If you are looking for a fun mindless action game, then look no further, given the price of the game this is probably one of the better values you will find. If you enjoyed God of War then you should check this game out as its the closest thing you're going to play on steam.

Thank goodness for Steam refunds, because the game really is that bad. I enjoy the Sims games and figured this would provide even a little bit of entertainment for me despite being very basic. I was very naive to assume so.
Pony World is riddled with glitches, two most notable ones being with the graphics (beach area, lake area and main menu rapidly flash white; this game should have an epilepsy warning)
One of the ponies I conversed with, called Lucy, was apparently so excited about spoken to she bounced around the town and then disappeared off screen.
Upon entering the forest my user interface became displaced and positioned near the center of the screen.
Broken game mechanic - if your health, condition and hunger decrease to zero your pony is completely screwed because it will not want to play mini games or work, which as far as I've seen are your only means of earning money. Fortunately, I was able to locate my save file and easily edit the values to restore my health, condition and hunger to 100 again and even give myself more money. Oh, and raise my job's pay amount.
The customization is painfully limited, the accessories are two items percategory: two tacky looking rump tattoos, 2 glasses and erm, two blankets. You can't even select different hair styles. The only other things you get to change is your pony body, mane and tail colour.
You can buy houses and even make a farm from different buildings like bread mills, wells, and vegetable patches. But you can't move or rotate any of the objects. If you dislike where your statue, flower bed or shower is, you'll have to delete your current one, buy another and place it elsewhere.
You can upgrade your knowledge and sociability by visiting entertainment venues like the cinema and museum, and strangely even by visiting the police and fire station. But since talking to other ponies seems to do nothing in the way of upgrading your friendships status (we're supposedly able to make our ponies marry and have children) it's completely pointless.
I do not believe for even a moment that this pile of rubbish "sold two million copies". It's a broken game. The function to marry and create families in the game is broken, the game's mechanics are broken, the graphics are broken and the developers want to make little girls cry.

The game itself isn't long; I started a new game, beat the levels (both regular and challenge) and earned all the achievements in 4 hours. I find it difficult to rate this game.  Eventually I decided on a positive rating since I am glad I played it.  Besides, I know how this works.  If you disagree with the majority, your review will be downvoted into oblivion and never be seen, even if you have good reasons for your negative rating.
While I have nothing but praise for
, Shantae and the Pirate's Curse is a mostly good game, marred by occasional bad level design and severe balance problems.
Shantae and the Pirate's Curse has fun abilities, great artwork and music, good humor, and sex appeal, just like the previous games in the series.  It is longer than Shantae: Risky's Revenge.
The only technical complaint I have is that it would have been nice to have the window scalable in windowed mode.  The developers have my thanks for adding key remapping.
As for general complaints about the level design and difficulty, there are many cheap hits.  Zombies often spring from the earth directly under you.  Ghosts often materialize on top of you.  These are an almost constant problem on Spiderweb Island.  The problem with Ghosts also happens on various other levels that include them.  When Scuttle Town becomes corrupted by dark magic, the Pumpkin Fields becomes black, except for the sky, making it almost impossible to see enemies or their projectiles, since they blend in perfectly with background elements like foliage.
There are several unique, and bad (uniquely bad), level designs.
On Spiderweb Island there is an area where you have to carry another character.  This prevents you from attacking or ducking, and causes you to die in one hit.  Some timing in this area is unreasonably tight.  The worst offender is the room where you are in tunnels with too little headroom to jump until you reach an area near the end with a platform overhead, and a kissing robot at the other end that is running toward you.  There is only a few pixels of space between you and the robot when you successfully make the jump, which will likely take many, many attempts.  This area is agonizingly long, like most of the problem levels.  When I play a Shantae game, I want to play a Metroidvania,
.
On Tan Line Island there is an area where you have to stealthily escape a palace.  This prevents you from attacking or using any special abilities, and causes you to restart the entire area if you are spotted once.  You are expected to make use of new mechanics, like blending into the shadows, without any explanation, and given the severity of the punishment for any mistake, experimentation is extremely unpleasant.  This area is agonizingly long, again, like most of the problem levels.  While I
stealth games (a lot, I am very fond of

stealth game.  The player has almost no means avoiding enemies other than moving out of their sight.  No distractions, no clever movement options, no disguises…  Making a mistake sets you back far too much.  When I play a Shantae game, I want to play a Metroidvania,
.
By far the worst area in the game is the Pirate Master's Palace.  The area is lifeless except for a few Bats and Save Guy.  It is mostly full of instant-kill spikes.  Like the other bad areas, it looks like it was lifted from other games.  In this case,
and
.  Like other bad areas, it is agonizingly long.  I died around 30 times in the first room before finding a way to bypass the first 3 rooms on Youtube.  After that, I was able to complete this area, but the process left me so infuriated and exhausted that I am unlikely to ever play through the game again.  This area officially “ruined the game for me”.  When I play a Shantae game, I want to play a Metroidvania,
.
The final boss is almost as badly balanced as the level he lives in.  Until I encountered him, I had avoided sacrificing any Heart Squid children to make Heart Holders.  I wanted to finish the game that way.  Unfortunately, each hit he lands is enough to instantly kill Shantae without any Heart Holder upgrades, and attacks like his bouncing cannon balls and flying pistols seem to be impossible to avoid even with a Bubble Shield.  9 Auto-Potions was not enough to see me through the battle.  Despite being squeamish about it, and it costing me the achievement, I melted all the Heart Squid children I found into Heart Holders so I could finish the game and write this review.
WayForward, if you are reading this, and I hope you are, please keep releasing more of this series, but make future releases fun, not frustrating.

Shantae and the Pirate's Curse... reviewed!

The story:
A Long Time Ago, before the first Shantae, someone called Pirate Master died and left a curse for Risky Boots, after Risky's defeat in Risky's Revenge, Shantae's Light Genie Magic became Dark Magic, and the Tinkerbats became Cacklebats. On a side story, Ammo Baron has bought Scuttle Town from the Mayor, who bought chocolate... Again. Now, Shantae has to team up with Risky Boots to defeat the Pirate Master, collect the Dark Magic from the Cacklebats and rescue Scuttle Town from Ammo Baron.
Pros:
- Shantae's adventure is now bigger, better and harder
- Awesome OST
- The characters are well developed
- Lots of collectibles
- Two different endings: The Good One, and the Bad One. I prefer to call them as Best Ending and Worst Ending respectively as there is almost nothing bad in the 2nd ending
- There's one Nostalgia stage with music from Shantae from the Game Boy Color
- Each boss has a different subtitle
- 4 different In-Game Wallpapers
Cons:
- That Last Dungeon is harder than anything else
- Dagron is harder than the Last Boss
Long Story Short:
Shantae's adventure is bigger, better and much more interesting but you still need to play the other games to understand most of it. So buy this game and buy Risky's Revenge

Superb game. Great gameplay, consisting of platforming, combat, and speedrunning, all coming together to create an incredibly fun experience. The story is compelling, being not too heavy, nor too light, while throwing in comedic moments and themes along with the more serious aspects. Sound quality itself is top-notch, and nothing more needs to be said about the soundtrack than to go download it on Bandcamp right now (it's free!). Art and animation are high quality, and I think a dramatic improvement over previous installments of the series. Replayability is high, and first-time players will find themselves with plenty to do even after completing the game, such as acheivements, wallpapers, and speedruns. Incidentally, this is the first Steam game in which I completed all acheivements.
Overall, 9.5/10 game, highly recommend.

The story is to survive, which is the most common theme, however, it does NOT focus on zombie killing. That's just a bonus. It's a story about how people need to survive off of each other when everyone's worlds  shatter collectively. Many needs can happen, people can experience bad memories, (especially when you have one of your teammates get eaten by a zombie then come back) and so much more. It's like Romero's movies. Sure there's zombies, but the worst enemy is the people who will do anything it takes to survive.
PROs:
*Customizable character creation
*Skills with a different trait for a given amount of points put into one thing
*Each weapon has its own stats (Some can break. Some weapons are improvised and shouldn't really be use)
*Stats are simplistic and easy to understand.
*The interactions of people and how they can survive in the world while trying to maintain their own sanity.
*The lifeness of each character (Each character has their own personality.)
*Animal companions. Have your animals help keep morale up or help defend your base!
*Situations that upcome and can change how people can view you.
Cons:
*Zombie AI. If there's a horde of them, they won't move one by one, they'll all move THEN get a turn to attack each of your characters. I understand these things operate on sound so using weapons isn't great. However, when a whole horde comes, it usually screws you over.
*Some characters are kind of useless than others.
*Story. LIke I said, it's more focused on survival and the desperation of people during the end of the world. However, if there is a main goal, I can't seem to figure it out.
*Combat is a bit awkward.
*If you're a graphic snob, aka, HAS to be 1080p and 60 fps, then this game isn't for you. The graphics are good, but not the best. Look for another game.
*The motorcycle gang members have super powerful weapons, even at early game, and can bring you down to half or a quarter of your health in one hit and when you DO kill them, their weapons dont have ANY ammo or any on their bodies.
Overall I would rate it 9/10. It could use a bit of work, but it is a great game. If you like the theme of the world turning upside down during the zombie apocolypse, and people doing everything they need to survive, then this game is for you. If not, try Left 4 Dead or some other game for your satisfying zombie head shots.

Dead State can best be described as Walking Dead Meets Fallout. With Brian Mitsoda of Vampire The Masquerade, this story driven game will let you decide if you are either a LaMOE or a Crusoe in this zombie shelter game.
The story takes place shortly after you wake up in the middle of a world that has gone to hell in Texas. After the cops found you and stitched you up along with two other survivors. You are tasked with at first making sure the shelter doesn't fall apart and take responsibility for the people that you choose to bring into the Shelter and make sure they have enough fuel, food and parts to get through each day in one piece.
As a zombie shelter game, there is notably less "railroad" situations where you will ineveitably lose allies. Theoretically you can end the game with every survivor alive and well when you finish the game unlike in State of Decay which ineveitably have you lose people to the zombies wherever you like it or not. That said, it's freeform so you can choose to be the few beacons of hope in a bleak genre or choose to bring out the worst in humanity as you kill those that are useless. Leave survivors to die or do internal purges after a mutiny by sending any member who was loyal to the mutineer to a suicidal march.
Combat wise the game plays like Fallout and Wasteland, an AP system that allows you to move and engage your enemy with a diverse perk system that gives you your own perks as well as other members of the shelter who have their own contributing abilities to the shelter.
The cast of survivor is a colorful mix from old war veterans, to an geek who uses the Fremen Battlecry or the avatar of Brian Mitsoda himself. Picking which survivor to come with you is important as some are illsuited for battle while others have limits to how far their moral compass will bend. A hint to know if your survivor has no qualms beign raiders is their attitude in combats. The more rough ones swear like a Borderlands player character and makes a nice addition to your motley crew of survivors.
Replayability sadly is lacking, while i had reservations about playing it again the lack of fulfillment in some endings have made me think otherwise for a great zombie shelter game.
Overrall I recommend this game for those who want their zombie survival fix.

MARLOW BRIGGS AND THE MASK OF DEATH is a 24-carat diamond hidden amongst the general crap that is the world of unadvertised B-games. Zootfly has managed to clone God of War into a game that is actually better than God of War, with a more interesting (albeit more racist) protagonist in a more creative setting and plot. The gameplay is fantastic, with a character action-based style of liner gameplay, and four very fun movesets based on the weapons you unlock, each with it's own set of satisfying combos. The environments convey an enormous sense of scale, and the camera tricks you into thinking things look much bigger than they are. The environments are very surprisingly gorgeous at times, and the graphics on the PC are surprisingly fantastic. The action is awesome and very over-the-top, with an increase in scale and buildup that rivals that of Platinum's action games, and the fighting levels are broken up by decently lengthy minigames throughout, including an on-rails shooter boss battle and a shoot-em-up helicopter section. Even the end credits are a minigame (which sure beats most credits sequences in terms of enjoyability!). The characters are just developed and fun enough to make a VERY STUPID, yet enjoyable and decently funny story, and the main villain, (also extremely racist) is a very satisfying enemy to face in the final boss battle. At 5 dollars, this is some of the best value you can get form a Steam game purchase, and it's a game that will offer you significant enjoyment no matter who you are. Trust me, this game stands out. Where did it even come from?
Just buy this game, it's great! Really worth taking a look at!

Marlow Briggs and the Mask of Death is a third person, hack and slash fest. It is perfect for the player who wants to experience a game that brings to life the feel of a classic action blockbuster film, over-the-top action and cinematic gameplay with a focus on relentless high-octane combat and danger filled exotic environments. As combo-driven adventure brawlers go, there's no earthly reason this should have gone under the charts like it did. I have no idea, but this game absolutely deserves a place with its AAA genre-cousins.
Marlow Briggs is also played the most known actor from the hilarious series Saints Row. I'm sure many of you know him from there as pierce washington, Dex and so on. But enough of me talking lets get down to the pro and cons.

Take God of War, remove it from ancient Greece and set it in South America, present time. Take all the cheese of 80s action movies, add the bravado and humour of those as well and you can pretty much describe Marlow Briggs.
It's a nice game when you just want to beat something up. Sure it's a budget title, and it shows at times with some questionable camera positions in a couple of places, as well as enemies which show up a bit too often near the middle of the game.
The jungle landscapes do look rather nice, the stop motion action sequences do a really good job of capturing the over the top action of some of the 80s action movies, without having to actually animate it. The combat is satisfying with your standard light attack, heavy attack, block and dodge rolls. Some rather good platforming segments and other action segments break up the game from being just beating up enemies.
It doesn't do much wrong. It's not exceptional either, but as a budget title it's a quite enjoyable time. Just make sure you play with a gamepad.

Medieval engineers is the second game in the engineers series by Keen Software House, after Space Engineers.
This review will touch on several topics concerning this game.
Table of contents:
1. Developers
2. Gameplay
3. Look and feel
4. Content
5. Stability and bugs
6. Conclusion (TL;DR version)
1. Developers
I think it's very important to address this first, since at the time of writing there's some serious accusations being thrown about. This game is NOT abandoned. The company, keen, consistently updates this game weekly, and since a total work ethic change a few months ago, became one of the most consistent, structured ones i've seen.
Updates are weekly on a tuesday, alternating between content updates, like new things to build, and bugfixing/stabilizing/optimizing updates. Once every few months, a major update is released, like planet-sized maps or farming/ores. i can't say i've ever seem them miss an update by a lot, unless they had a very good reason for it.
2. Gameplay
Medieval Engineers plays like a mix between a survival and sandbox game. While the survival part has been traditionally rather barebones, improving on this has been the team's focus for quite some time now. Farming and tech progression are just some of the things the team has added to make this a richer experience over the course of the last year.
As for the sandbox part - Medieval engineers isn't story-bound and allows the player to create whatever they want - there's also a creative mode to omit the survival aspect entirely for those who purely want to focus on building magnificent structures from the get-go. Despite the presence of creative mode, survival isn't compromised, and everything you can build in creative can be built in survival.
3. Look and feel
Medieval engineers, just like space engineers, takes a mostly realisti approach in it's visual style. the game is quite detailed but as a result does put a bit more
4. Content
At this point, medieval engineers has a pretty decent ammount of content. there are still things both major and minor that are desired to be added, but there's definetely enough for a base game. While vanilla itself already allows one to richly decorate buildings from the inside and outside, both in terms of furniture and architectural variation, the modding community definetely helps by adding things that are too specific in taste for the game to automatically have for everyone. That is of course, not to say the mods fill the holes that the game leaves unfilled, it just adds those niche things that are more of an expansion than part of what would make the game whole.
5. Stability and bugs
I am aware that this section can be rather personal, and that's exactly why i beg your consideration when taking this in account while rating the game. the thing about bugs is that they're not always consistent. I personally haven't encountered any bugs that made me frustrated while playing. (honestly, i can't say i've encountered one recently at all), but i know that other players have. However, it's safe to say that at the moment there's no game-breaking bugs that are widespread across larger part of the community, or if there are, they are usually fixed in one or two updates. the dev team has dedicated every odd update entirely to fixing bugs and stabilizing and optimizing the game.
6. Conclusion (TL;DR version)
In my experience, medieval engineers is on the right track. It still has a way to go to reach it's full potential, but is definetely showing both promise and the will to move forwards. the game is pretty solid at this point, and it doesn't seem like the dev team is stopping anytime soon, with terraforming being the next major update set to release soon. While it definetely made a very slow start, it's picked up speed since 2015. i have to admit that i entirely quit playing somewhere in 2015 because the game was progressing so slowly, but when i came back to it a couple of months ago, i saw that it had grown into something far greater than what it was then. i think that given time, this can be a really solid game, and it's already pretty neat to play.

As i saw both games on steam, i knew that my choice of buying them
was the best choice i ever made. Long story short with the history of me and
Shantae, the gameboy game was a great part of my childhood, and i wouldnt be here reviewing the games
without it.
In anycase, seeing both the new games on steam, i bought them on an instant,
as i knew that the games where made by the same guys, so i knew it be a
great experience, just like with the gameboy color game.

Here is my review of Pirate's Curse. Similar to Risky's Revenge, it has the same sprites and graphical style,

any transformations, but isntead, gives you artifacts that gives you new abilities, while the belly dance was

Again, Kodus to the developers of giving my childhood game new life, and a great experience

One of my favorite games from one of my favorite series. I love the Shantae series and this is possibly it's best one. A great platforming game and entertaining with the characters within. Shantae was Ret-2-Go in the first 2 games but this one will definitely suck you in. I'd suggest trying Risky's Revenge, but if you dont feel it suits you, jump into this one. Simplest way to play is via a gamepad. I hope you all will love the Half-Genie Hero as much as I do.

Shantae and the Pirate's Curse is a 2D metroidvania platformer adventure. You play as Shantae, the half genie guardian of Scuttle Town. Recently you have lost your magical powers, but you don't let that stop you from saving the town once trouble comes through. Most of the trouble is caused by evil magic being sent out by the imprisoned spirit of the Master Pirate. It's your job to team up with your former rival Risky Boots in order to stop his minions, collect the magic, and prevent his spirit's escape.
The gameplay is fairly simple. You can run around, jump, duck, crawl, and whip your hair to attack. Along the way you will receive new items and upgrades to give yourself more abilities and more power. You use these abilities to access new areas in order to find secrets and progress. There are a few light puzzles and fetch quests sprinkled in, but the main play will consist of traversing overworlds and conquering dungeons. You can also increase your health and carry items to heal you on the go or to give you some other battle assistance. You'll need to skilled in combat, platforming, and adventuring to complete this game.
The music is overall pretty great, being polished and interesting to listen to. The art is a mixture of two styles. The playable game consists of colorful pixel art that is well animates, while the dialogue bits have hand drawn cartoonish representations of the characters. The sound effects are also an interesting mix of higher quality voice and sound sample along with retro style video gamey effects. The controls are tight and understandable. Plus, the dialogue is cute and can actually be funny at time. It's an interesting mixture.
For those who played Shantae: Risky's Revenge before this as I did, you'll be glad to know that nearly everything has been improved upon in this game. You get lots of new abilities rather than just recollecting the same ones from the previous game. The story is even more interesting with the same quality of dialogue. The hand drawn art is different, but it seems to have a bit more detail. This game has more length, with more places to explore, things to do, things to find, people to talk to, and just generally more everything, which means even more quality playtime. The difficulty is also higher for those looking for a greater challenge, which is welcome since this is a sequel, but not too hard for newcomers that would like to try it as well. The map system has been improved to read more like a standard metroidvania style map and show you where you have and have not been. If you liked exploring, platforming challenges, puzzle challenges, combat challenges, and just the overall gameplay of the previous game, you'll love this one even more.
There are a few issues with the game though. One that may have just been for me was that sometimes there was a flickering glitchy effect on some backgrounds. This usually only happened in the company logo right away and on the world selection screen, but it also did happen consistently in one temple where I kind of needed to know where the walls and floors were. It was only for that one room in the one temple, but it kept happening after a few reloads so it may be a real problem for others as well. Also, I didn't think the cartoonish characters hand drawn in dialogue scenes meshed well with the pixel style of the game. Mayb it's just me, but I would rather just keeping it all one way. That's minor. The difficulty could be a problem. It's harder than the previous game, which is good for people who played that first and it's not TOO hard for those who want to jump right in, but to some casual gamers it could be a bit too tough to get through. While I like that the map system has been reworked and the sailing aspect works will with giving Risky more purpose, it's a shame that instead of one big interconnected world it's now multiple smaller worlds you have to select separately.
Overall, Shantae and the Pirate's Curse is awesome. If you like metroidvania games, it's a great one. If you played the previous game (which I also reviewed on here) and liked it, this is definitely worth looking into. It's a fun, metroidvania adventure platformer with a pretty style. I like how fun, challenging, and yet forgiving the game is to make it a lot of fun to keep playing. Another one of the best games I've played on Steam. Is it worth the 20 dollar asking price? Well, personally I would say that, if you're really interested and liked the other Shantae games, then of course. Otherwise maybe wait for a sale. I got it for 15 and it was worth not being able to wait anymore. If nothing else, getting it at 10 bucks or less at some point is going to be a real steal, especially for all the content here. Shantae and the Pirate's Curse gets a 9 out of 10 for being a great blend of genres, gameplay, personality, and style. Also... I know I'm a pervert but... I mean, come on, Shantae is a babe ;)

This game is extremely mediocre, and while that's not necessarily a bad thing, I personally want more out of a game of this price. It's a perfectly fine way to kill a few hours, but it's nothing special, and I certainly don't think it's worth $17.
My main complaint is that the game tries to hard to be funny, but it just isn't. Its jokes, which are almost entirely references (some of which stopped being funny a long time ago) nearly always fall flat, and there's just so many of them. If the game had more going for it this wouldn't be such an issue, but it doesn't. There's nothing really wrong with the game mechanics (aside from a few issues I had with selling weapons in one of the areas), but I found the story really uninteresting.
On top of all that, I don't really understand why the game is about potato people at all. I get that it's trying to be unique and memorable, but the 'incredible potato world' thing really doesn't improve the game in any tangible way. That's kind of a problem.
I've heard HPAWS described as soulless, and honestly, that's probably the best way to describe the game as a whole. HPAWS tries so hard to be fun and quirky and cool, but it doesn't pull it off, and in the end it's just kind of tedious. I don't think there's much replayability, other than maybe playing the game over again to see how much quicker you can finish it the second time, and with an estimated 5 hours of gameplay it's so not worth it. 5/10, play Recettear instead.

Star Wars Republic Commando is one of the franchise's many forays into the realm of FPSes, a genre which it manages to do surprisingly well considering greats like the Dark Forces/Jedi Knight series. This game does remarkably in that regard, offering you an honest mix of weapons and gear to engage the enemy as well as a good few levels and a strong overarching story to hold it all together. Its main claim to fame is a squad command feature, which is actually one of the best I've seen in any game. Your allies react to your orders and interact with each other in very amusing fashions, as each one is fleshed out into a character of their own. Fixer, the gruff, no-nonsense hacker. Sev, the solemn, sociopathic sniper. Scorch, the funny, wisecracking demolition expert. You'll grow to appreciate your 'brothers' over the course of the game, as well as the intense, fast-paced action. You'll face a lot of challenges on the way, but you're a commando...it's in your job description.

One of the few tactical shooters I can stand, also happens to be one of the best Star Wars games in the galaxy. The shooting may be a bit dull, there may only be a few weapons and you can finish the story in one night if you have nothing better to do, but there's an odd charm to this game. The characters certainly help this by being pretty distinctive and interesting; both the voice acting and writing is top-notch. The story is pretty standard Star Wars fare, but because the lead characters are clones it's a lot less "YOU GOTSTA STOP DER SITH!!1" and a lot more "HOOAH!" In addition, the graphics still hold up well thanks to their stylized realism. Although repeditive at times, the levels are pretty great and you'd have to be as dumb as a womp rat to get lost in them. Lastly: retractable fist-knife? Coolest. Weapon. Ever.

One Piece Burning Blood is not only a really good fighting game, it also is one of the best One Piece games up to date, featuring close to 40 playable characters and featuring twice as many as a support cast, therefore spanning almost all relevant characters throughout the entire series.
The game itself plays like a tag team brawler, different characters have vastly different movesets, combos and special attacks have really nice animations and most battles feel very impactful, don't drag out and are neither too easy nor too frustratingly challenging.
The art design captures both the visuals of the manga as well as the anime quite brilliantly, the story ark of Ace's execution is a bit lacking both in depth and length, but uses many quotes and reenacted original scenes from the books / anime, which are extremely satisfying to watch being brought to life in 3D.
All in all I had a lot of fun with this, the only downside was a minor technical one: The game doesn't allow for 4K resolution and tabbing out of the game or losing window focus automatically disables fullscreen, which resulted in my game window being quartered a few times when I got popup notifications through Windows and where I had to finish the ongoing battle before I could re-activate fullscreen again. Apart from that, it is a completely solid port, immediately recognizes a 360 controller and shows the correct button layout without having to fiddle around.
Definitely recommendable to both One Piece as well as fighting game fans alike.

This game is so bad even the devs don't wanna play it.

- Some really interesting bits of writing
- Too many NPCs bug you about nonsensical things ("Stop taking me out into the field!" when I'd never actually done that)
- Combat has few tactical options. You can't take cover or delay your action.
- Too often you are forced into ridiculous fights (15 zombie on a narrow road with the only exit on the opposite side)
- During a fight, the active character cycles between EVERY character on the entire map. Even if they're not active or near you. In some maps, after your guys take a turn, it can take almost a minute of just watching it cycle through zombies that aren't active and do nothing.
- The turn order is useless for know when a specific enemy will move since their portrait is only loosely related to their in-world model
- There's an option to show which containers on the map can be looted (most can't). This is off by default, and turns itself off each time you play
- There are horrible glitches in how it renders area with multiple levels. When on a map like that you will often see people floating in air, or have the ground below you disappear
- You can tilt the camera, but only very slightly which makes it hard to see certain areas that you want to move to
- You can get "Status effects" like poisoned, bleeding, etc. These are shown by an icon, but there is no tooltip when you hover over them so you have to look them up in the manual.
- The pathfinding is bad. It will show that you can't reach an area, but if you click a few squares at a time, you'll get there
- If you want to move to a square that contains a corpse, you need to carefully target around the corpse.
- Having the Science skill means your melee attacks inflict Poison. What?
- When looting it shows you how much you are carrying, but not how much you can carry.
- The game maintains a To Do list, but even when you complete them they will often not be crossed off
- In combat, facing is important but you have no way to change your facing
- Weapons have special attacks, but there's no way in-game to see what they are. You have to go read the manual.
Overall, it's unpolished and unfinished. If you can get it on sale, it's still worth picking up and trying. I wouldn't pay full price or recommend spending the time to finish the game once it starts to drag.

I really, really wanted to like this game.
I’ve been watching it for a long while and started playing around Halloween. I am a big fan of turn-based games, base-builders and the zombie apocalypse-survival genre. Dead State is mature in theme and has a lot of different luxury goods to try and keep your group happy
Dead State is a graphically good looking game, but unfortunately one rife with bugs.
There are typos, and floating inventory items – but these minor issues which can be over looked. A big problem in the game for me was when I had started building the well for my base. My project leader became sick and had to take a day off from working on it. When she returned to work the next day, the game refused to recognize that any of my characters possessed a crowbar, which was deemed a requirement for the task. I equipped her with three, in every imaginable slot. Nothing seemed to appease the game. While I was frustrated, I was determined to play on.
The Coyotes are a violent, enemy group of rival survivors and they are VERY powerful in the early game. After several attempts to defeat them (there were no diplomatic options) I decided that you had to run from them. The Coyotes fire their weapons discriminately in combat and the sounds draws wave after wave of undead reinforcements down upon you.  Added to this, there are situations where, in combat, your move options are limited by fallen companions, KO’ed foes, terrain and areas of control of standing combatants, effectively trapping your characters so that they cannot fight enemies, while your foes continue to pump you full of lead. In tight spaces this can be lethal for your group.
I finally quit in frustration. I really wished that this game could have been more polished.

I purchased this game with high hopes from reading other reviews, but was ultimately disappointed. After a few hours of play I don't feel the game is really as described in its marketing.
It seems that Dead State is mostly about crafting and shelter maintenance, with some exploration and combat (and some other negative reviews have described the awful combat system already). These are things I have zero interest in. I was hoping for the "social management" and "narrative" parts to be stressed more. Instead, there appears to be no story at all, no narrative, nothing driving the game save for the shelter.
While this may be realistic in a zombie apocalypse survival scenario, I just hoped for more in the way of RPG and less in the way of "scavenge small items and make something out of them." This would have saved it from being as slow and boring as it turned out to be.
As an aside, there are also numerous bugs with the tutorial text appearing to give you tips about things you did 5 minutes ago, or are no longer in the room for, etc. More care needs to have been taken with editing and overall experience by the player.
Totally disappointed, although someone else more interested in crafting a shelter could find this game fun.

Who says that all low budget-games are crap? Marlow Briggs proves that this is not always the case.
Despite the low budget, the game boasts an amazing presentation on par with most AAA-games.
The gameplay is also really fun, a lot like God of War in a good way. Not only is the combat and platforming really fun, with great controls and a great variety of weapons and combos, but there is also variety in gameplay-styles, so things don't get too repetitive.
The story itself is really simple: Save your girlfriend from her evil boss.
However, the aforementioned presentation and the characters really make the experience very enjoyable.
Marlow Briggs himself is a very badass and likeable character (not to mention, a rare black protagonist that isn't a stereotypical gangsta), and King Tep, the titular Mask of Death, is a hilarious companion, with praise going to Steve Blum's funny and over-the-top performance. The witty conservations between them really makes the characters memorable, not to forget the hilarious despicable villain.
The only negative thing that I can think of, is the fact that you can't change the graphical settings, so people with not-as-powerful computers/laptops are going to have problems running the game at a decent framerate, unlees you change the resolution.
In short, a very enjoyable fighter with a b-movie-feel, but in good way, since the game itself has fun with it.
If you like games like God of War, and enjoy movies like the ones Michael Bay makes, then Marlow Briggs and the Mask of Death is an awesome game :D :D

This game is a low-rent "God of War"-esque game with a South America Aztec/Mayan theme. During my playthrough I ran into multiple camera issues (camera flew out of the level and I got treated to the low-res backgrounds until I restarted the checkpoint, among others). The platforming is okay, but there are a few times where it's difficult to tell where you're supposed to go. Likewise, I ran into a few sections where the camera moves while you're supposed to be moving and it threw off the jump, leading me to more than one unfortunate and frustrating death.
That being said, the game has pretty decent humor and it knows its place in the game pantheon. It doesn't try to do anything special, and there are the same basic weapon and magic sets you should expect to find in a game of this type.
Overall, it's a decent game. With a short playthrough (roughly 6 hours on normal) and some aggravating camera issues, I don't know that I would recommend it at full price. If you're looking for a cheap, quick hack & slash game with decent humor and a nice, new setting then I'd recommend picking it up.

Wow.
If you're played Risky's Revenge or read my review of the previous Shantae game, it's a pretty rough entry into the platforming genre. Pirate's Curse is, in turn, a vast improvement.
Though it retains the same sprites that were used on the DSi, the resolution is much sharper, with crisp, attractive backgrounds and new animations thrown in. This also makes the HD graphics used for conversations and menus a lot less jarring, but they still look a bit odd at first. Though enemy sprites are reused from Risky's Revenge, it also adds a lot more of theIt also has a lot more enemies, and new huge, screen-filling bosses help make hitting the end of a level a lot more exciting than before.
Shantae feels faster, jumps farther, giving a better feel to the controls, and her speed and leaping ability grow dramatically as you go through the game. Unlike the "lock and key" transformations of Risky's Revenge, which often don't see much use outside of opening up a new zone, you'll find yourself using most of the equipment which replaces the transformations in regular gameplay. The extra movement options also make traversing zones a lot easier. This time, the zones are connected through a central hub, and you readily can get items that return you to the hub. The exploration is much improved, though it still struggles a bit (being able to warp directly to dungeons, for example, would have saved a lot of tiresome trekking). The levels are now quite varied, often with different gimmicks other than just graphical stylings.
It's also a
funnier, and... might I say fairly fetishy by comparison, expecially during the early parts of the game. If that kind of thing bugs you, it will bug you. While it's not
Totally Spies, some pretty odd fetishes feel like they're checked. I just find it amusing, but others might find the humiliating nature of some of the situations more problematic. Still, the dialogue is far more clever than earlier iterations, and generally got me to at least crack a smile at some of the back-and-forths.
Even those "stop 'n go" enemies I hated from the previous game are improved. For example, Riskys' Revenge had mermaid enemies that would try to bore you to death through periods of invulnerability, but now their windows of invulnerability are now far briefer. In addition, often Shantae can dispatch enemies much faster... or, later in the game, just heedlessly charge through them or float over them. Magic has been replaced with limited-use items, though in some areas they drop often enough you may as well use them all the time. Overall, it's a clunky system compared to refreshing magic, but it's not a real black mark.
Ultimately, Pirate's Curse is a lot of fun. Where Risky's Revenge relied mostly on charm and nostalgia for appeal, Pirate's Curse has a lot more substance. It often has different sequences where it offers variations on the core gameplay to keep things from being too monotonous, and the new equipment keeps shifting how you play the game. Thumbs down on a final level that suddenly kicks up the difficulty drastically and frustratingly, but at least is capped by a very satisfying end boss.  Though it's not a breakthrough or a massive innovation in the genre, it's a very solid platformer that feels and plays great, and gives me a lot of hope for the upcoming HD sequel.

This is what I call an improvement!
If you check my profile, you can see that I played and reviewed an earlier installment of the series: Risky's Revenge. While it was lacking in some aspects it was cool enough that after the convincing gameplays I decided to jump back to the series. This is definitely more fun and polished game and I can easily say it is worth your interest with only few hiccups along the way. If the game is solid, then I'm more than happy to nitpick some issues for further ironing out for the next Wayfoward's game. Criticism makes excellence!
Game is notably faster than the Risky's Revenge. The previous game was pretty sluggish at times, but the improved controls, Shantae's speed and jumps in pair with good level design, help dictate a reasonable pace that makes you flow through the game with no noticeable frustrating moments. Graphics are in my favorite 16/32-bit Mega Man X4-rish style, that didn't really change after Revenge (with recycled sprites), but it still looks pretty nice, especially with the new locations. Bosses are definite plus. While not very challenging, they provide fun encounters. There are a lot of new faces as regular enemies which are good to see. Platforming? No complains there.
Music deserves an separate paragraph. Jake Kaufman did probably his best score yet. In my opinion it's far better than Shovel Knight's and provides tons of catchy memorable tunes that really "sells" the game. I would say that without this soundtrack, many locations wouldn't be as fun and atmospheric as they are now, since many of them are pretty generic. Mud Bog Island with Village of Lost Souls hidden within it is an great example of climatic location boosted by an amazing music. This stuff rocks.
The story. Characters are likeable and unique, scenes are full of humor and plot overall isn't particularly offensive, but...
Logic? Out of commission. Setups? Wasted potential. Lore? Barely touched.
It looks like the devs had a plenty ideas for funny situations and hijinks between characters. There are lots of mini character arcs that bring this thing together, but logic behind why scene A resulted in events in scene B is completely bizarre. It fits the convention and style, but for me it is something of a missed opportunity. Keep in mind that this is a nitpick and Shantae doesn't need a great story to be an awesome game, but I would say that this is an aspect for further improvement.
Upgrades. They are all powerful and really fun to use... unless we are talking about the Sword upgrade that is only useful for unlocking vertical shafts and nothing more. It gives no advanced mobility and is pretty weak against enemies. No sense in using instead of standard hair whip. Pistol and additional melee attacks also become obsolete really fast, but other upgrades are extremely fun to use and tinker with.
As for a completely minor sidenote, which doesn't hurt the game that much, but I would like to point it out... There is also a strange dissonance in level progression vs. classic Metroidvania mechanics. Shantae controls would really shine in level-to-level progression system (intro level shows this), but this series was very exploration heavy from the start. Game tries to bring the best of both worlds, but levels are not-seamlessly connected and they are overall pretty small, so there isn't as much exploration as in standard Metroidvania and there are not enough set-pieces as for classic platformer. You can really feel it, as the game has less adventurish feel and yet doesn't deliver as much level-specific excitement as Freedom Planet or Shovel Knight. Luckily, this is subjective and not very noticeable. It doesn't affect the enjoyment as much, probably thanks to the overall solid experience crafted by the devs.
The only proper negative that I can think of is the price. Content-wise, it offers a similar about of fun and features as afromentioned Shovel Knight and Freedom Planet, yet it's price tag is 5 dollars higher. 15 bucks is a perfect price for fun and enjoyment you will get from Pirate's Curse. It's solid platform game that is definitely worth your interest since it holds up a great quality on par with other genre representatives. If you are a platforming fan, then you are making yourself a disservice if you won’t put it on your wishlist!

is a short-and-sweet, casual, side-scrolling platformer.  You won’t find anything groundbreaking in it or much innovation at all, but it is a fun game.  If you enjoy casual puzzle-platformers, and you want a new experience, then you will probably enjoy
.
It’s a simple game, with the main system to solving levels revolving around the 2 basic mechanics: splicing your DNA with animals to gain abilities (flight, underwater breathing, better jumping, etc.); and creating clones of yourself which you can then take control of.  The puzzles are simple, and the platforming is easy.  It is a very casual game.
Each level has some collectibles and a par-time to beat; they are very generous and easy to achieve.  It won’t take very long to earn 100% completion in the game, and after that there isn’t really much replay value.
The graphics are mediocre, and there is not really a story or anything.  However, the controls were good for me with a controller, and there were no frustrating parts.  I experienced no glitches/crashing.
Having said all that, I enjoyed my playthrough of
.  It is certainly far from the best game in the genre, but I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys casual, side-scrolling puzzle-platformers and is looking for some novelty.  It is a short game, though; but if you get it for a good price, it is worth the playthrough.

A pleasant way to spend a few hours.
Pros:
+The Base-building Aspect is a lot of fun.  The delicate mix and interplay of facilities, resource management, and character skills including your own definitely play a big impact on your crew's morale and survival prospects.  Those who get bit (infected) during the game as a result of combat with zombies have to be managed with daily antibiotics.  Each infected cause a potent little morale hit on a daily basis (fear those infected will turn keeps your survivors up at night).
Wounded characters heal in user built infirmaries.  Recovery in HP can be slow, fatigue is implemented if you have your characters scavange the wasteland of Texas for too long without granting them rest, and the additional game modes with the most recent "Reanimated" update even make it possible for your own character to get infected.
+The Reanimated patch adds a few of the more interesting game settings to the original base game that ramp up the zombie threat to 11 without making it impossible and human enemies are much more aggressive and damaging if you elect to ramp up to Hardcore game mode.  The Ironman mode I wouldn't recommend given the occasional save game related bugs in the game but if you save often there's no problem with anything else.
+The large map and variety of buildings is almost varied enough in their experiences to wipe away some of the larger pacing problems.
+Some characters that can join your fledgeling community of survivors are extremely interesting characters in their own right so there's enough variety in the mix of personalities on display in this game to intrigue the imagination.  Its a pity that the NPC banter and dialogue for each of these characters (~30 altogether) couldn't be fleshed out a bit more than it is but its good enough assuming you are patient enough for their scripted events to come to you.
+The Crises events in the game add a lot of tension to the game and the amount of democratic support you have leading up to these events as well as the consequences of your decisions to resolve the crises are well thought out.  Its a pity there weren't more Criseses to help with the pacing problems that occur in the mid-game.
+Pick your favorite picture of any flesh-toned animated flavor and your enjoyment and immersion into the atmosphere of the game will automatically increase by leaps and bounds.  The portraits that come with the game I found - disturbingly - androgenuous especially for the men.  The game lets you import custom portraits...use that.  The rest of the NPC characters portraits are perfectly fine though so don't let that deter you.  Its only the PC that looks...questionable, shall we say?
+The game allows you a broad choice of presets background and skillsets and lets you choose your own by assigning points how you will.
+The other factions in the game will definitely reach out and make their presence felt. Some will be hostile, some neutral, and some will be friendly.  A few will change their status depending on your words and actions.
Cons
-Graphics and animations are good enough for an indie game of this type but there's nothing you would call clean or flashy.  I don't mind this one very much just thought I would toss it in to cover my bases.
-Ambient Music track is super repetitive and the one combat song gets real irritating real fast. Play some of your own music in the background and crank the music volume in the game down very low unless you really love the unimaginative midi drum-beat ambient deathrattle.  My zombie kill-count went up immesurably and I had a lot more fun when I turned to my own combat mix.  Yours will too, trust me.
-No voice acting
-A pity the infected mechanic doesn't have a stronger thematic element than merely a morale and daily biotic hit beyond the fixed three day incubation period of Zombie turning.
-The dialogue after the introduction that you initiate in your community shelter is weak and repetitive outside of scripted events.  This is one area that may be the most disappointing from a narrative standpoint.  Each character gives you something to worry about and do and they will get into conflicts with each other in somewhat realistic fashion.  They will even group themselves into factions under sub-leaders you come across which is also nice but the lack of depth in the dialogue still makes me find this game to be a flawed gem cut too early in the development cycle to reach its prime potential.  The indie budget shows most severly in this area but the early game has the most content and in all honesty I found the early part of the game in the first month to be the best most fleshed out part of the game by far...
-The factions also suffer from a lack of fleshed out developement. They are interesting and do interact some but there is a gap between what is realized and the potential that might have been realized with more time and money. More diplomacy and more varied interactions and scripted events would definitely have helped the pacing problems in the mid-game.
-Pacing problems. The greatest content is at the start when you are busy trying to set everything up and get recruits and resources to deal with opening crises and character conflicts but this dries up in the mid-game pretty fast leaving you scavaging and fighting the remaining areas on the map until the scripted end-game sequence leading to the finale and one of the game's true endings.  That's all there is to say, I'm afraid.
Summary
If my hour count is any indication (I bought this game when it first came to steam early access), then I have certainly gotten my money's worth a few times over from this game.  It took a very long time for my interest in the game to wane and it certainly improved technically and qualitatively from a gameplay standpoint from its most recent reanimated patch.  Nearly all of the game related bugs are long gone by now and the game itself is a lot more tense and exciting with the hardcore and PC infected options enabled from said patch.
My only real disappointments with the game largely result from the fact that they simply did not have more than a matchbox budget to start with from their modest kickstarter and that has certainly plagued this game's development for a very long time.  That said, I remain quite fond of this indie game company and its devs for the hours of tense enjoyment they have given me since this game's release to Steam for early access and what they accomplished with such a small low-budget.  The indie team are, IMHO, very passionate about their work and considerately attentive in regards to their community.
For all its flaws and rough edges, this game is amazing in its concept, focus, and scope.  Nearly every other game on zombies boils down to a button mashing action kill fest but this game takes a more cerebral approach to its gameplay mechanics where the focus is on survival not just of your one avatar or a few NPCs but an entire community of folks whose problems go far beyond the basic humdrum of scavanging and NPC questing.  The game doesn't deprive you of either or from simply going toe to toe again the zombie hordes and the diverse medley of surviving human factions.
Bottom Line: This is an amazing little game for such a small indie team.  Excellent Concept, decent implementation, a good mix of features that are especially rare for a genre plagued by first person shooter fare.  You'll also find far more meaningful choices than can be found in any Telltale Game.
Its rare for a game of this type to hold my interest for as many hours as I've logged into it over the years; so yes, I would definitely recommend this game in its most recent incarnation without reservation to any fan looking for a more cerebral Zombie Survival RPG game that casts you as the Headman of a small community of quarralsome survivors struggling to survive the Horrors of the Apocalypse together.

Dead population, clear lack of balance, some characters are just pure cancer that people just spam the same skill over and over, and the DLC characters are quite obviously OP, the connection is better than the garbage that Naruto games are, but that's not saying much at all.

- Locked to 30 FPS
- Alt tabbing while in full screen will force windowed mode. You will have to go into settings to revert this
- Constant online connection issues.
- FMV cutscenes can audio desync
- The art style for this game for is not very good. The "pencil sketched shadows" effect looks slapped on
- Character animation in the main campaign's cutscenes are stilted and of low-quality
- Basic tutorials, no combo trials/challenges, and no advanced tips for characters
- Combat is sluggish, shallow, repetitive, and restrictive
- Attacking in general takes forever to startup and to recover
- There is unresponsiveness and/or delay with moving, jumping, or preforming directional attacks
- Spamming certain moves are encouraged, as several character-specific attacks are safe on block, can't be punished consistently, and do tons of damage
- Story-relevant character abilities (Logia, Haki, etc.) have no drawbacks, and make sets of characters objectively better than others. They feel tacked on, they take the enjoyment away from having a clean even match, and they really don't improve or add anything of worth to the already mediocre core gameplay loop
- "Flash Guard" and "Flash Counter" mechanics reward players with no risk involved, as they cost nothing to preform. They seemingly exist to artificially make CPU opponents more difficult, as they will use it whenever they feel like interrupting your combo
- There is no grabbing in this "fighting" game. The alternative, guard breaks, are not a good substitute. They take forever to startup, and are very easy to avoid, and punish. So blocking or dodging everything becomes overpowered. Other
fighting games have it so if you block enough, your guard will break naturally. Why this game doesn't is beyond me
- Guard breaks are supposed to be beaten by normal attacks. Sometimes a guard break will recognize a attack string and will be beaten in response, as it should. Sometimes it does not. The fact that everything has so much startup, delay, and recovery does not help anyone

- 1 vs 2, or 1 vs 3 matches are not balanced. In fact, there is no benefit for playing a solo character in a match, at all. You don't get any health, defense, and/or attack buffs to compensate. You do not get meter faster. You can't do meter-specific options, as they require a team. There is no solo/single character meter-using options, other than going into super. You don't get any more EXP or in-game currency, or unlock any achievement for winning any match solo
- You can only have a max of 3 support characters. If you're playing solo/single, for instance, you can't use the extra "Team Points" to fit in any more support characters to compensate for the fact that solo/single matches are not balanced in your favor. The "Team Point" system seemingly exists because the developers knew that certain characters were overpowered, and chose to implement this, rather than fix the fundamental balance issues that make this game frustrating to play
- Characters can level up. It is not explained. What does leveling up do? Why does it exist? What benefit does it add to the game? I'll tell you: if you're playing a low level character, higher rank CPUs become nearly impossible to beat. They have too much life, and do too much damage. It makes the game a mountain of a challenge to beat with skill alone
- The game's "challenge mode", Wanted Posters, has a grading system. It is harsh and frustrating to get high grades. Why? On top of dealing with the generally terrible, unbalanced combat. You have to not get hit, and finish matches quickly. Most CPU will be content with sitting around blocking all day, waiting for the moment when they can spam the moves they have that can kill you instantly. A large portion of Wanted Posters force you to play with characters that you may be unfamiliar with, and are not good at. The biggest issue with this mode is the fact that you CANNOT RESTART A MATCH. You either have to let the CPU kill you, or quit a match, wait until your dumped into the selection screen, and try again. This would not be a complaint, if you not for the fact that you CAN RESTART IN THE MAIN CAMPAIGN. Why did they forget to add that quality of life feature to this mode, where the bulk of the single player content lies? Your guess is as good as mine
- "Flag Battle Mode" is not explained at all. I can barely find any resources explaining what it is and how to play it on the internet, even
- There are no alternate colors or outfits for characters, with the exception of a handful of story-relevant ones. You will have to fork over the money to buy the DLC if you truly itch for some variety
IN CONCLUSION:
There are better One Piece games you can buy
There are better "anime" games you can buy
There are better fighting games you can buy
There are cheaper games you can buy, that play better, and are not locked to 30 FPS
And for the price of this One Piece: Burning  Blood, you can buy several of those games
Please use your valuable money to buy something else
