What is Dead State?  It's a game that does a similar premise to State of Decay, but in a different way. I managed to beat the game after 79 hours of play, but managed to defeat it on my first try.  There is a bit of grind-y nature to discovery, looting and zombie-battling.
All in all, though, I enjoyed the game enough to play through it entirely to see it through.  I did lose interest around Day 70 and more or less had to power through the next 20 or so.  I don't know if I'll play it again since I was sucessful.  I can see if someone doesn't manage to beat it wanting to try it again, though.

underneath, there is a golden experience. I give this development team full credit and surely don't agree with anyone stating after -20 played hours 'game has been abanded' or something like that. The enemies are not designed at all for the gameplay as some would require flanking but everything is too cluster-phobic or require too many AP to do it and because of the of the randomness you may or may not have a shield pricing or ignoring weapon that will do enough damage. Enemies also do ridiculous amounts of random damage, sometimes just scratching them or out right kill them in one hit so when you do flank it just places you in a worse position.
The combat is made even more awful by the fact you can’t shoot on the diagonal which burns the already random number of points that are sometimes so low you can’t do anything with them and moving through your own marines consumes even more. Better hope your random weapon is useful because you might as well you harsh language. Punching has knock back but one square means nothing and you were better off blasting them instead of wasting a AP on each side. Your guys are generally so weak both offensively and defensively moving solo or away at any distance is going to get them killed.
The level generation is just horrific. It’s far too tight, slapdash and at times require you to bust down walls just to get to the exit. Enemy placement is absurd at times leading to whole room stuffed wall to wall and you hoping they don’t have enough random AP to get to you. Then there are random events that just leave you ???. Moving through each level is a slow and painful process as moving at speed will get you killed. You constantly have to setup ambushes which slow you down to a crawl and even if you are safe the slower marines will drag you even further.
The levelling system is barely a thing. You get new skills but most are not particularly useful and your stats don’t seem to increase. You don’t feel anymore powerful than before.

A short, well paced walking simulator in an exceptional interesting setting with strong focus on story telling and dialog instead of exploration and with a nice crafted story that kind of looses its magic at the end.
Honestly, it took me a while to decide if i want to recommend this game. There are some elements of the game i really enjoyed and thought they were really great, but a lot of those elements also had their downsides.
I absolutely loved the game design. Radiant atmosphere, colors, sound, models, ui, gameplay - i think it looks truly artistic and unique. But while the playable area seems like a big, beautiful and interesting landscape, you soon will figure out that there are actually all small areas with only 1 or 2 ways to go and are just too restricted in interaction or exploration. Sometimes it didn't make sense why Hank wouldn't be able to jump on a small rock when he just climbed a much bigger one couple of minutes before.
I really liked Hank and Delilah. The way they talked to each other was fun and immersive through the believable voice actors. Their interactions are limited to talking over the walkie-talkie and i think that must be tough to write and act out so the players would enjoy it through the whole game. if this part of the game would be boring, the whole game would suck. Instead you have the feeling to know so much about Hank and how he must feel that you sympathize with him almost immediately.
The controls with the walkie-talkie are easy and felt really good right from the start. Doesn't matter if you play with mouse + keyboard or a gamepad. I liked the fact, that i could almost always choose what Hank should say and it resulted in a dialog that felt natural and believable for the situation Hank was in.
The story develops slow at the beginning but that suits the sad curcumstances Hank is in and it felt the pace was always on point and it actually felt longer than the 5 hours it took me to finish the game. But besides that it disappointed me somehow at the end. I think all the decisions you made don't actually matter at the end and thats a shame, because i enjoyed the dialogs. For a short period i was totally hooked and thought the big mystery in the story will be more mind blowing but it was rather predictable and i felt somehow misled.
Worked smoothly on ultra settings without any bugs, crashes or anything else. UI- and in-game actions worked without any troubles.
Seriously, ♥♥♥♥ this game and everything it stands for! I wish I could still get a refund for this glorified clicking simulator.

I've been playing F2P Devilian non-stop since it's come out. I've ever only made one other review, but people seem to be sh*tting all over this game with less than 5 hours of gameplay invested, so I feel a more informed point of view can be of more assitance.
The game genuinely feels like Diablo and WoW mixed into one game. The first time I logged in I was greeted with a chat system where people weren't spamming like idiots. I had players running around me in the enviornment doing the same quests as I was. Yes, the mob respawn rate is very high to offput the number of players killing them. This, however, is countered by a short 'de-aggro' range, and taking damage does not knock you off of your mount, which by the way is free within the first hour of the game. I never spent more than 20 seconds waiting for a chance to activate a quest point, or wait for something to spawn so I can kill it.
There are only 4 classes in the game, but each has 3 different talent trees, which you can assign points to as you wish. I chose the Marauder class, and as such my three trees were AoE damage, Single Target Damage, or Tank-ish. It essentially turns the game into 12 classes, instead of 4.
The combat is fast paced, there are a bunch of different areas your quests take you to, each having dungeons located within them (though not the only way to get to the dungeon, as there is a dungeon finder queue), along with multiple difficulties. Ranging from Normal, Medium, and Hard. While those aren't the actual names of the difficulties, they might as well be. Medium and Hard are your end game to get gear, to my knowledge. Some of the bosses in normal dungeons were hard enough. You'll have to deal with dodging abilities, cones of damage, bombs on the floor, etc. I only imagine it gets much more difficult (and fun) at the higher difficulties.
The quests themselves aren't anything spectacular, what you'd expect. Go here, kill that, gather this, do this, that, etc. They're fast, mostly easy, and a good source of experience. I'd be a little more upset with the questing system, but it's saving grace is the auto-run feature. No, not in a straight line. Auto-run to exactly where your quest is. In fact, you can open the map, right click on a place, and you're off.
The different zones I've been to so far seem to vary in theme, some snowy, some firey, some jungle, and even desert.
You don't spent too long in each zone, maybe 2 hours depending on how fast you work through it. It's definitely a grind to get to max level, but I'm already nearly done after a few days.
So. Do I recommend this game? Yes, I do. I didn't look at the reviews as the game came out, didn't research it, just played it for what it was, and I'm having a blast.
So, let's talk about some pros and cons.
Pros:
-Easy, rewarding combat system
-Auto-run to quest locations
-Minimal fighting over mobs/objectives
-Frequent world events
-Mostly non-toxic community
-Mix and match talent system, creating tons of character options
-Quick leveling experience
-Easy to learn crafting system
-Challenging dungeons
-Full game without paying a penny
Cons:
-Limited player inventory
-Exp / Money % boosts through in-game store payed with real money
-F2P accounts cannot trade with each other (from what I hear, don't quote me on that)
-While large zones, everything feels like a tight squeeze
-Players often rewarded with "megaphones" that let them broadcast 1 message per megaphone to entire server
-Definite pay to win vibe, but ultimately paying will not make you stronger than a F2P account.
Don't listen to the 1 to 5 hour reviewers. Spend time in a game before you trash it.

At first glance, it struck me as an interesting idea: playing as a shop owner, managing your shop, researching better weapons, etc. However, the actual execution of the game is extremely lacking. After about 2 hours of gameplay, everything is just a repetitive grind.
First off, all weapons from the same category has similar patterns of stat growths. For example, all Daggers have high speed and magic. Thus, there is a single "Best Weapon" in any category, and if you've already had that researched, there's no real purpose in researching the weaker ones other than for completion.
Secondly, the research mechanic is totally boring. They could have made an interface allowing people to "craft" certain weapons by combining relics, but instead they went for a no-depth waiting mechanic, where you just wait for your item to be done.
To add to that, the explore mechanic ruins the management aspect of the game. You never run out of materials anymore as long as you send your explorer out every month or so. There's no purpose in having shops around the world since your explorer gathers items for free. You end up completely drowning in materials that you don't really need.
Not to mention, some of the objectives require the player to gather a sum of money, and as soon as the player has that exact amount, the game takes it away from the player. One time, it left me completely broke that I wasn't able to pay my hired smiths on the payday.
All in all, the game had overcomplicated things that could have been simple (such as the general shop interface, the world events), and overly simplified things that could have been expanded and made interesting (such as the research, exploration, and general weapon-making mechanic). There are better games to spend your money on.

After finishing the game, I can honestly tell you that this is one of the best platformers I played in years. Compared to Risky's Revenge, this is like 100x better, so if you liked Risky's Revenge, this one is a must buy.
PRO's:
- Perfect controls - never had a fail jump or miss-shot due to controls
- Fun and addictive game - the characters are fun, as-well as the story and you will hardly get bored while playing
- Graphics - a pixelated masterpiece. The characters and environments are rich in color and animation. Not one zone looks the same as another
- Music - what good is a game without some quality music? Each zone has it's specific tune, some new, some remixed from previous titles and will set the perfect mood for each stage and situation
- Gameplay - this is the major improvement over the last title.  They mixed the diversity and complexity of the 1st game with the quality of Risky's Boots and they managed to obtain a solid and lenghty game. When I completed the intro and saw that this game is composed of multiple islands (stages), I snapped my fingers and said to myself: this is promising. One hour later I was drooling at how awesome this is
CON's:
- If you want to gather all the hidden items, you will need to write the progress down a paper, because the game informs you of this only on the stage (island) select screen
- The inability to tweak the volume and customize the controls...hopefully these options will be implemented with a future patch
Final Thoughts:
Does it worth the full price? Yes! It's one of the few games that I bought it at a full price and didn't regret it. So, if you want a solid platformer, with awesome gameplay, characters and story...then don't look further.

Well this is a huge step up from the previous title, Shantae: Risky's Revenge. This game take place after the events of Risky's Revenge, so if you haven't played it and don't want to be spoiled stop reading the review and go play it.
Shantae is trying to remain guardian of Scuttle Town as a full human with no genie magic. Risky come in and tell her that the Pirate Master is returning and they must band together to stop him. The story is nice and got some good developments/reveals for the side characters. I personally like Rotty Tops backstory in the game. It may not be an award winning story, but it good enough to keep you entertained to the end.
The gameplay is the same in the previous game. A side scrolling platform where you whip you're enemies into submissions. In place of the animal transformations from the last game, you will now use pirate items to help you progress through stages and defeat enemies. If you’re looking for a fighter with a solid, interesting roster, then One Piece: Burning Blood is right up your alley. But, if you seek story and new insight from your anime-based games, you will be left wanting.
PROS
+Great roster with lots of variety.
+Combat dynamic is well executed
+Simplistic Controls
+Well-designed Characters
+Frantic action and tons of eye candy during battle
+Overall cel-shaded presentation is very true to the manga and anime
+Tutorials & simple-to-remember controls make for accessible fighting action
Cons
-Short campaign's story
-Repetitive even for a fighting game
-30fps lock
-New players will be completely lost with the story
-The camera view during gameplay allows for bigger characters to cover too much of the screen
-AI can be unbelievably dumb at times
-Random difficulty spikes make completing certain objectives a frustrating chore
-Story recaps the events of the series in a way that's incomprehensible to the uninitiated
It goes without saying that existing fans will get the most out of this one, but fighting game enthusiasts should still find some fun in exploring the nuances of the title's combat system. On the surface, Burning Blood is an accessible brawler that's built on a pretty standard rock-paper-scissors foundation: quick, normal combos beat guard breaking attacks to the punch, guard breakers smash through your foe's defences, and blocking nullifies regular blows. It's simple stuff at first, but once you factor in perfectly timed guards, sidesteps, heavy guard breakers, unique special attacks, and aerial offensives, things quickly become much more complex.
In terms of combat, One Piece Burning Blood does a good job of empowering you with spectacular fighting skills, no matter which character you opt for. In the same vein as the aforementioned Naruto games or the recent Saint Seiya brawlers, you take your chosen character(s) into battle, and attempt to put together a successful series of attacks.
With Square and Triangle as your main attacks, things feel pretty comfortable within moments, but the addition of ranged attacks, special moves, guard-breaks, tag moves called Unity Assists and Breaks, and the powerful Awakened state add extra depth that could easily have been missing. It’s never going to trouble any of the more technical 3D fighters, but there’s still a lot to grasp.
There are intense difficulty spikes at points in the campaign, which often rob proceedings of their fun, and I wasn’t sure whether the fact that every character levels up with use – they’ll still advance slowly without it – meant that I was simply at a disadvantage from the off.
One Piece: Burning Blood suffers from one of the worst things you can these days, repetitiveness. It’s evident in the gameplay, the story mode, and even the characters you fight while playing online. The top tier has kind of already been established, and players are quick to flock to it because they want a win. Ultimately your victories are won because you played better defense than your opponent, which runs counter to the bombastic nature of the One Piece series. Sure you can throw out all the wild attacks you want, and they’ll look really cool, but they’re also easily avoidable, and counterable. The lack of depth is what kills what should have been a really fun game, and that’s a shame because the effort to make this game beautiful is there, it’s just a shame the gameplay didn’t receive the same effort.
Final Verdict: 2.5/5 passable

A short, well paced walking simulator in an exceptional interesting setting with strong focus on story telling and dialog instead of exploration and with a nice crafted story that kind of looses its magic at the end.
Honestly, it took me a while to decide if i want to recommend this game. There are some elements of the game i really enjoyed and thought they were really great, but a lot of those elements also had their downsides.
I absolutely loved the game design. Radiant atmosphere, colors, sound, models, ui, gameplay - i think it looks truly artistic and unique. But while the playable area seems like a big, beautiful and interesting landscape, you soon will figure out that there are actually all small areas with only 1 or 2 ways to go and are just too restricted in interaction or exploration. Sometimes it didn't make sense why Hank wouldn't be able to jump on a small rock when he just climbed a much bigger one couple of minutes before.
I really liked Hank and Delilah. The way they talked to each other was fun and immersive through the believable voice actors. Their interactions are limited to talking over the walkie-talkie and i think that must be tough to write and act out so the players would enjoy it through the whole game. if this part of the game would be boring, the whole game would suck. Instead you have the feeling to know so much about Hank and how he must feel that you sympathize with him almost immediately.
The controls with the walkie-talkie are easy and felt really good right from the start. Doesn't matter if you play with mouse + keyboard or a gamepad. I liked the fact, that i could almost always choose what Hank should say and it resulted in a dialog that felt natural and believable for the situation Hank was in.
The story develops slow at the beginning but that suits the sad curcumstances Hank is in and it felt the pace was always on point and it actually felt longer than the 5 hours it took me to finish the game. But besides that it disappointed me somehow at the end. I think all the decisions you made don't actually matter at the end and thats a shame, because i enjoyed the dialogs. For a short period i was totally hooked and thought the big mystery in the story will be more mind blowing but it was rather predictable and i felt somehow misled.

Steam Marines is an interesting squad based rogue-like where you roam a steampunk ship with steam marines as besieging enemies attack. You sweep levels dispatching robots and aliens, and boss enemies that guard the exit to the areas at the end.
The key aspect of this game is that you are leading a group of marines, from which each will have their own tactical uses. You'll have different weapons equipped and different abilities to use - each which will require specific positioning to make the most of.
There are also a variety of areas to move around in too. Initially you'll be moving through the Command Deck which will feature basic Robot Enemies to fight off. After beating the Command Deck you'll be able to pick what area you wish to move onto.
Of course, you are probably wondering where the unfavorable part of this review comes in, so let's get into that now...
Difficulty levels don't seem to be balanced well for inexperienced or experienced players, RNG elements seem to be in places where they shouldn't be - like how much shops will sell stuff for or what they sell or in starting attributes of your marines.
Progression is also a rather annoying aspect of this game. You start out in the Command Deck everytime you begin - but it will get sterile quite quickly. Areas feel a bit expansive and long, which is fine, but what isn't fine is that you are moving through 5 levels for each area. When moving through the levels, it is possible for you to spawn next to the elevator - and if it is the last level of an area, you will spawn next to the exit boss....
There were also some general annoyances such as skill balance selection being extremely unbalanced - leaving to little choice in what you pick. I also found that the enemies can be somewhat unpredictable in some situations - which is not a good thing to have in Rogue-likes since it is part of the game to understand how enemies operate!
Really this should be an enjoyable game, but its chief problem is that it feels like it hasn't been fleshed out enough. I haven't seen any re-visitation from the developer though, so I feel that this negative review is warranted.

Look, you may have heard bad things about this game zbut frankly, this is a game i'd call not that bad. Like with Dead Island, how you view it depends on how much you like zombies. As a game for those who enjoy zombies in survival horror, it's an 75-85/100, for everyone else lower that score about 15-25 points (and 60 is average). First of all it's a linear campaign designed for Co-op that's also playable in Singleplayer if you like choosing the lesser way to play the game. (This is NOT as the case was with Dead Island where both were enjoyable and challenging, the game is legitimately made for Co-op and not much more.) There is yet to be a survival mode nor has one been promised but don't let that disuade you, as the campaign offered is much better than you may expect.
Now if I have to say this game's greatest strength out-loud other than the kill-cam, it's how it handles hordes and this game is somehow able to handle hordes of slow zombies better than any game i've ever seen, and yes that includes Left 4 Dead where zombies were basically lightly wet sponges in comparison. This is admittedly something that has to be seen in action or played, and at that in co-op as singleplayer scales the zombie count down considerably. I myself haven't run into too many bugs nor any game crippling ones other than the innability to adjust player voice chat volume in the options menu. I can't put it any better than this: If you are find paying $20 for an Okay game and love zombies to death (and hopefully have friends who feel the same) this probably a pretty good purchase for you. It's legitimately tense during many moments and as I said before handles hordes better than any zombie game i've ever seen. And just to set the record straight, they did actually appear to put a bit of effort into this.

An excellent example of a good horror co-op game. While it may be not the perfect game (it has some glitches and bugs) and definitely the story isn't the best there is around, it's still a very entertaining game, with a lot of hours of fun in it. I mean, after all, it's SHOOTING NAZI ZOMBIES WITH YOUR SNIPER, what else do you need?
Graphics are more than okay, the shadowing is PERFECT (these are the best shadows I've seen so far and I'm not making this up, they look REALLY realistic). When you shoot a zombie it plays a slow-mo animation following the bullet and showing you how the bones and organs of the zombie you shot get pierced by it as the bullet goes through its body, so that adds a nice touch (Sniper Elite v2 has the same animation but with live soldiers- well, not live anymore since you killed them, but well, you still get what I tried to say).
And finally the controls are excellent and easy to use.
Overall, it's an excellent game to play with friends, and if you're speaking with them through Skype, TeamSpeak or RaidCall then it's waaaaaaay better!

Marlow Briggs and the Mask of Death is a shining example of story and emotional conveyance within a video game's narrative, and you're missing out if you haven't already experienced it.
In this gripping tale, Marlow Briggs is abducted from a 3v3 basketball pickup match by gray aliens from the planet Xernov. With their language comprised mainly of "ayy"s and obscene laughter, Marlow manages to understand that the aliens wish for nothing more than peace with mankind, and require Marlow to be their middle man.
In one of the most masterful combinations of interactive cutscenes and interactions with dialogue trees, Marlow suddenly and quickly is fallen by an ancient evil awakening. This Summer, Marlow Briggs must team up with the Xernovians in order to defeat these elder gods once and for all. With some of the most fast-paced and intense rhythm sequences since Beatmania XVIII and iDOLM@STER, Marlow must jam and slam his way up the corporate ladder in order to become CEO of Time Warner Cable and provide a stable internet service that reaches across America that doesn't tug ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s in its spare time.
Myst? Forget about it. Dear Esther? You'd be DEARly mistaken. The Last of Us? That takes last place. Gone Home? Check this, not your privilege. Marlow Briggs and the Mask of Death provides one of the most cinematic and moving moments in the  entire history of video games that I won't dare spoil. Here's a hint, though: Marlow is forced to choose between his love of futbol and the security of the Patriots project. Which will he choose?
Citizen Kane? More like Citizen Lame. Buy Marlow Briggs.

You play as a female viking warrior who died a dishonerable death and has to prove herself to the norse gods (the Jotun) to be able to enter Valhalla. It's a BEAUTIFUL hand drawn 3rd person action-exploration game with fantastic presentation and quality.
You explore the areas finding the runes and fighting the bosses. You're fed the back story of Thora as you progress. Along the way you can collect Ithunn's Apples, which increase your lifebar, and you find the god shrines which grant you with god powers such as healing, shields that surround you and protect you from damage, Thor's hammer, ect... These powers help with the boss fights and are a welcome veriety to the combat. Each of the areas have a different gameplay mechanic or environmental thing you have to deal with like being frozen by the blizzard winds, or being burned by the lava bursting through the cracks in the ground.
The controls are simple and straight foreward with a normal attack and slow heavy attack, as well as god powers and a dodge roll. The gameplay is a little bit slower, Thora runs and swings her battle axe kinda slow. Durring boss fights when you get an opening to attack you might only get 2 or 3 swings in. It's not a bad thing, I actually enjoy the pace of the gameplay, especially with how fast and twitchy a lot of games are now.
The boss fights are unique and varried. They're absolutely the highlights of the game. If you're a fan of Dark Souls and other games like it, you'll enjoy the boss fights. You have to study and learn the patterns, know when to attack and when to stay back and evade attacks. The beginning of the fight is pretty easy but when you do enough damage, the boss brings out new moves and changes things up. I love it. You can tell they put a lot of thought and effort in to each boss. Plus the hand drawn animations are gorgeous to watch.
The game was a little hard to get into at first because it doesn't really tell you what to do or where to go in that first area. You're just supposed to explore around and you'll figure it out. You learn the game by just playing it. I got a little bit lost and confused navigating some of the levels because the map is pretty vague. It gives you a basic idea of what the area looks like but doesn't identify where you are on the map. The level where you walk on the tree branches was tough to navigate. If you enjoy these types of games you should definetely check it out.

I received this title as part of a bundle, but the idea of playing the other side of the item shop seemed neat so I gave it a shot.  The game makes clear quite early that you're expected to pour your time into it - perhaps that's what the "casual" moniker means? Either way, after crafting a dozen weapons or so, and opening up a new location, I decided I wanted to get off of the ride.

If you liked Game Dev Tycoon you'll likely like this. It takes things in it's own direction but the template is clear for you to see.
Some of the humour seems to have been lost in translation but it's a harmless relaxing management game with pleasing visuals and dopamine zinging stat bubbles.

The good things about Jotun are the very pleasant aesthetic and music, greatly increasing the flavour of the "walking simulator" parts of the game. References to the myths are sadly quite shallow, which means the game works best for people who already know the folklore, as opposed to those wanting to get into it, Might spike your curiosity, but that is about it.
The sad part is that the game opens fantastically - the first level teaches you everything you need to know about the mechanics of the incoming boss without explaining anything in text, everything is fully intuitive. The fight is balanced to be thrilling, but not painstakingly hard and the limited moveset gives it more depth thanks to the need to time your attacks and opportunities.
Then, the game opens and I am not even sure if the player is supposed to tackle the bosses in any specific order or not; the special powers sure are distributed quite unevenly. I did the clockwise direction of clearing the encounters, which means I defeated 4 bosses before getting two final skills. Very weird. Also no idea if the enemies are scaled at all to your progress in the game.
The main problem, though, is that every boss-fight beyond the first has some real problem with itself. Actually, scratch that, the Ice Jotun was actually really sensible. As much as an enemy who turns his entire arena into slippery ice can be. A little annoying, but still fair.
Others, however...
- Thunder boss is the most drawn out fight of the entire game. Long, tedious and not very exciting. Doesn't help that his main source of damage  (which he uses sparingly) requires a ton of concentration, isn't that easy to get evasion of right and obliterates your health bar quite fast. And then there are two of them, which is... not a great phase two. Especially since that means even more dancing between thunders
- Fire Jotun is sooo close to be good. He is relatively interesting, requires many different patterns of dodging and intensifies the fight as it progresses in real, tangible way. So why do I complain about him? Because he comes as close as the game does to instakills. In phase two his sword attack (pretty telegraphed, but still can hit you at times) not only does obscene amounts of damage, but it adds an AoE fire attack. Which you will be knocked into upon hitting. That disables your ability to move for a brief moment, during which you receive damage, and then you still have to walk out of that fire. While it damages you. Unless strongly upgraded and on full health, this hit ends the fight
- Stone Jotun uses some nonsensical mob of dwarves to make fight tedious; the creature itself is barely any dangerous, so the entire experience is pulled towards annoying lot of adds that... well, how much does anybody like fighting endless stream of adds? The fight becomes a game of ignoring the helpers as much as possible.
- And the final boss is... well. Homing Attack, the Boss. That is literally the main thing, throwing homing attacks that do not dissipate until they hit you. The more you dodge, the more of them will stack flying around the arena, leading to inevitable situation where either you realise this is happening and activate shielding power, or you are pummeled to death. This would make the fight merely boring, but given the fact that he can summon AoE powers of all the different bosses,
, it becomes impossible to understand what went through the heads of the designers.
In the end we have shallow, not overly satisfying exploration married with shallow, not overly satisfying combat. The game tries to be a walking simulator and super-hard-game-of-bosses at the same time, and fails at both.
Sit this one out.

Midieval Engineers is made by the same company as space engineers and in a lot of ways is strikingly similar. There are a number of differences though. The primary difference appart from setting, is the survival mechanics. While playing the survival mode of this game you do not start with the full knowledge of the different crafting materials or building materials. Instead you must research the different technology teirs to progress farther. In my opinion this mechanic is something that propells the game forward and prevents it from stagnating and resulting in a fatigueing issue that i so often have in space engineers.
Another key difference is the introduction of structual integrity. This prevents you from building structures that have no means of supporting themselves. This makes the game feel not only more realistic, but also more flushed out as far as physics go.
Pros-
-Fun sandbox experience
-Lots of exploration
-Regular updates and development schedule (Every Tuesday)
-Stunning graphics and beautiful scenery
-Many more building features than that of space engineers
-Better keybinds than space engineers
Cons-
-Requires a decent ammount of power to run reliably
-Still many bugs due to the alpha build status (NOTE: I do not hold anything against the title for the alpha build status and while i am aware that the number of issues in the game i currently have are directly related to the development cycle of the game and its alpha status, i do believe in reporting on anything and everything that would change or otherwise impact the experience of the player)
-The UI is clunky and awkward to use
-The UI is not very intuitive (Devs have stated UI changes are on the way)
-Character controls feel stiff

When I first bought this game in 2015 I guess I could say I overhyped it as it was a predecessor to Space Engineers which I enjoy also, unfortunately back then it felt like a total scam with such a lack of things to do.
Now though, 2 years later Medieval Engineers has evolved so Incredibly well.
The game follows basic sandbox principles. Gather resources, create a base of operations, and survive. Surviving is fairly easy with the only real threat being the odd bandit or two, or if on multiplayer other players. However food can be a real hazard early game as most raw foods you gather are barely nutritional and won't keep you going long. It's only until later stages when you can farm that food is more manageable.
Progression in the game is simple and fun though can be a little of a grind at times. You progress through by gathering resources and using a research table, 'craft' them into research scrolls granting access to Masonry, Iron Works, Defensive Structures, Farming, etc opening up new building possibilities.
Considering this game is still early access it's worth the money and it's amazing watching this game grow. The only downside really of this game is heavy PC requirements in certain situations such as huge structural collapse (yes you can knock down castles it's glorious) and a few bugs here and there, but that to be expected.
I give Medieval Engineers a 9/10 for creating an amazing medieval sandbox game

I'm a huge fan of things medieval...I'm also a huge fan of Keen and think they're the best, most honest devs out there who always listen to players and add things in their games they never planned on doing themselves. That said, I'll try not being biased. I'll also try keeping this from being too long.
ME is early access...that you should know immediately. Though it's not complete, it has a fully functioning Survival mode with at least some decent amount of content that's more than just harvesting resources to build with. Along with that, here's a more detailed list of some things currently in game (which will probably change tomorrow and the week after and so on):
-real physics. Watch castles and towns crumble to the ground under their own weight or from projectiles hurled through the air
-a failly detailed crafting system...i.e. gather iron ore for smelter, take ingots to smithy, grab sticks and other objects from the forests and ground to complete items, ect.
-Houses and banners which make online a lot more fun especially for role-playing. Gather your friends under one banner and declare war on enemy territories.
-voxel based terrain to modify worlds or builds in creative to come up with endless creative ideas
-grid-based construction that's also dynamic...this isn't like Minecraft. You build single structures on their own grid, but different structures can face any angle you'd like
-Farming! This is a nice recent addition to the game and greatly enhances survival play and playing with friends.

This is honestly a must-buy if you liked Pandemic 2, but wait for a sale. It's a really fun game, but it's a bit overpriced at $15.
Make no mistake, the game you're buying is Pandemic 2 turned up to 11, and the developer worked hard to create a ton of variety to try to keep the game from getting stale. If you like Pandemic 2, you will like this game a lot. If you don't, you won't.
Pros:
- Lots of different types of plagues, each with varying properties. Some vary more wildly than others.
- Several special plagues that are not remotely similar to ordinary ones. These include a zombie apocalypse, a Planet of the Apes plague, and a Vampiric outbreak
.
- Lots of traits that that subtly change your plague (mostly little stat buffs) for flavor, and you need to unlock them which encourages replay.
- Awesome mod support that lets pretty much anybody create their own plague using easy-to-use tools.
Cons:
- Some of the different plague types feel really samey, and many of them can be beaten using the exact same strategy.
- The plagues are not different enough in terms of available symptoms, with the majority of plagues all having the same ones to choose from. Why not switch it up a little?
- Some of the special plague types can be a grind.
- A lot of the game involves waiting, and sometimes the spread of your disease can feel painfully slow. If there was a very, very, very fast game speed option, I'd use it,
It's a fun little game based on a popular flash game, and it does enough to provide plenty of content to make it worthwhile. And with the mods available, there's pretty much a never-ending stream of different scenarios for you to play.

And I gave this game an 80%
(VALUE 40/40 for its $5 USD price tag, FUN 25/30 considering the games target audience (kids).. I can see this game a lot of fun to them, CONTROLS/BUGS - 10/20 I would like to see game add arrow keys and WASD controls to move and minor glitches but nothing game breaking, and GRAPHICS & SOUND gets a 5/10 for being nothing amazing, pretty simple, but also nothing horrid awful either)
Value and Fun are always my two biggest criteria when I grade a game, and in this game - I have to put myself in the shoes of a young kid.  I figure the target audience here is kids from the ages of 5 to 12 (mainly girls but some boys my like it as well)  The Value is out of the park in this game.  For $5, there is a LOT here to offer a child.  They can make friendships, once those friendships blossom they can do more such as play ball with them or comfort them, and once it blossoms further, they can give them gifts from their inventory, and eventually can marry them!  Add in the ability to have baby ponies, and OMG.. how could a young girl not LOVE that?!!?
The fun level I believe for the games target crowd is going to be at least a 25 out of 30 because this game offers again so much.  besides making friends as I mention above, the player can get a job, shop, explore, play simple games for money, while all the time needing to keep their energy up, their cleanliness/self appearance bar up, and their hunger bar up.  They get to use their money to build their own stables home, decorate it however they choose, grow crops, and much much more!  Awesome.
While I wish the controls allowed for movement with the arrow keys or WASD key movement, moving is as simple as clicking where you want to move, or holding down the left mouse button to have your pony follow the arrow as you move it around.  A few glitches such as sand colored too brightly and a screen that would sometimes be off center but then later correct itself will likely be rectified in a future patch, but I had to score this aspect of the game down a little for it.  It's not game breaking at all, just a minor set back.
And the graphics and sounds are really simple but they work is why I gave this part of my score a 5 out of a possible 10.
You can save the game at any point and go right back to it easily by just clicking the play button.  Unfortunately, it doesn't look to have multiple save spots available for more then 1 child.. I would definitely love to see the developers add at least 3 save spots to this game.
Again, this game is not targeting 16 year old boys, or 30 year old men.  So don't buy this if you are over the age of 12 and then trash it because it's "lame".  Doing so would only prove your own ignorance.
Awesome value for the money for a younger kids game, and I can see lots of younger girls specifically loving this one!

Oh, man, where to start...
I love the Shantae series. Big fan since the first game, and it just gets better and better. Pirate's Curse stays true to the controls and platform gameplay of the first two games, but includes new ways to attack and navigate. Shantae can no longer transform, but the items she finds in her adventure feel just as natural as her transformations.
The enemies are a combination of those from part 1 and 2 plus new ones.
And the music, oh god, the music. Jake Kaufman, composer for the previous parts of the series, as well as Shovel Knight and Double Dragon Neon, is again responsible for it, and it is awesome. Fans of the earlier Shantae adventures will even get some familiar tunes.
If you still need convincing, listen to my annoying voice while playing the game:
TL;DR: Just buy it, man.

These are the pros and cons I have come up with during my first full (100%) playthrough of this game
+ I have never taken so many screenshots in a single game before
+ Platforming
+ Artwork
+ Soundtrack
+ Plot (not just the story...)
+ Humour in almost every cutscene
+ Death barriers are clearly marked so you know which holes are hidden rooms and which aren't
+ Lots of achievements
+ Didn't feel like I was missing too much backstory even though I have yet to play the previous two games in the series
- Two of the three combat skills you can buy are basically useless compared to your standard moveset
- Maps do not tell you which items you have already found (and where they were located) which can lead to excessive backtracking
- All the achievements are making my OCD kick in
All achievements acquired update:
+ The speed run achievements are quite the challenge and the game rewards you with two "fan-service-y" wallpapers if you can beat it in under 2 hours with any% and under 3 hours with 100% completion.
Completed and acquired all achievements for Shantae: Risky's Revenge update:
Pirate's Curse vs Risky's Revenge
+ More bosses
+ More dungeons
+ Less confusing map system
+ Risky's ship and pirate flares replace Warp Squids (much more convenient travel than before)
+ Twice as long to complete (not counting Pirate Mode)
+ Movements and attacks are faster and more fluid
+ More meaningful dialogue and story
+ Artwork of characters has improved and looks more like a visual novel during dialogue
+ Save files now display %completion and location of last save
+ Different attacks do different amounts of damage instead of them all being considered one "hit"
+ Better quality and more memorable music (the soundtrack is also twice as long)
+ Graphics settings now allow true fullscreen (no black bars or stretch) for 1080p monitors
+/- Graphics are more or less the same as Risky's Revenge
+/- Weapons and items replace transformations and magic  (I personally like this game mechanic but some people would prefer the hallmark transformations of the previous Shantae games)
Shantae (GBC) 100% complete update
Its kind of funny how I ended up playing this series in reverse order... Now on to the update:
Pirate's Curse has many references to the original GBC game. Many of the songs heard in this game are actually remastered from the old chiptunes of Shantae. While the original game was MUCH more difficult in terms of travel from one area to the next, I feel like Pirate's Curse was a nice change from most of your troubles being day travel (or rather NIGHT travel when enemies were twice as tough) to more emphasis on labrinths, quests, bosses, and overall story.  I still think Shantae is one of the best GBC games out there so don't discount it just because I said Pirate's Curse is better. If you ever do get a chance, play Shantae (GBC).
Verdict: Buy it now out of 10

I bought this game for the story and comedy. Yup. I totally did not buy this game just for the fan-service. That's right, just for the story. That round, voluptuous story.
Edit 4-26-15
Now that I've beaten the game, I believe it's time I gave it a proper review.
Difficulty: 8/10
The game is not too easy, and not too difficult. The puzzles are challenging, sometimes needing you to think outside the box to accomplish it. The enemies are well placed in the stages, preventing you from mindlessly steam-rolling through the stage. There are a lot of secret areas too, which rewards you greatly if you find them. The bosses are fun to go against, each requiring their own strategy to beaten. Plus, they get faster as they near death, increasing the challenge.
Art: 10/10
The design of the characters are amazing. The way they're drawn, the personalities given to each character, the dialogue, it's quite astonishing.  (and maybe you might even add one or more of them to your waifu collection). The enemy art is also great.
Music:10/10
Each piece of music is a magnificent work of art. It meshes well with the stages their associated with. I recommend playing earphones, even if the game doesn't.
OVERALL: 9.5/10
If you're interested in challenging platformers, quirky characters, great music, and a memorable experience, this game is for you.

Steam Marines is a great concept that never got finished.  Many of the poor gameplay elements, admitted to by the Dev, were supposed to be changed before launch.  They were not.  Dev swore all over the place that he was going to maintain the game post-release, and not abandon it the day it came out.  That's exactly what he did, leaving TONS of game-breaking bugs and glitches.  There is no music, there is no variety, the tutorial in no way prepares you for the amount of missing information you'll find in the game.
It's sad, because this really could have been a great game.  It is not.  It's a twenty dollar turd that you should avoid at all costs.  Dev skipped supporting this game to start working on a sequel instead, but that's a dangerous road.  How many people are going to buy another game from someone who just got bored with his first one and left it to rot?
You can still see the 'road map' on the discussions page.  After playing the game for a while, then reading the road map, you realize that a vast amount of the features the dev decided to leave out are exactly the ones that needed to be implemented to make this a great title.  I have no idea what he was thinking, because he was well on his way to making one of the best games to come out of Greenlight/Early Access.

I was expecting a "traditional" tactical RPG, but this is something different.  Normally I like experimenting with new & different things, but I wasn't a fan of how things were handled in this game.
The movement system is strange where you use directional arrows to move characters around instead of pointing and clicking. If you press into a wall, that actually takes an action point.  This is because you can break through pretty much any wall.  Changing your facing consumed an action point, which I consider an unforgivable flaw.  This is something I'm used to being "free" in all other TRPGs.
There is no story at all.  There's nothing between each level.  It just jumps into the next level as soon as you finish one.  The goal in every level is to reach the elevator.  You don't have to kill all enemies.  The enemies are unbalanced.  I played at the easiest difficulty and I encountered several enemies that I couldn't cause ANY damage on.  That includes blasting it with my "heavy" and nearly killing himself with the splash damage.
It felt like a random demo that someone made to show off their gameplay system.  There is nothing tying it all together.

I’m not entirely sure what you can expect from such an obvious low budget videogame. But being fun isn't one of those things normally. This game is surprisingly solid both mechanically and its story, even if it takes neither of those things seriously. The effort put in shows. Sure, the game’s plot is as 2-dimensional as a standard platformer and the character's don't have much of a backstory but it's pretty darn fun. Especially when you have a SHMUP sequence thrown at you and doesn't feel out of place. The game switches between action spectacle and puzzle/platforming to keep things moving.
You follow the adventures of Firefighter Marlow Briggs who gets killed by an industrialist voiced by the noodles guy from Kung Fu Panda. (It sounds like him and I’m pretty certain it is, but the credits don't say and IMDB doesn't credit him with the part). The guy who is voice acting him is clearly having tons of fun with the role. There is so much ham and cheese to his villany, you can't help but giggle. After being resurrected by a Mayan Mask of Death, Briggs must fight through hordes of enemies and gods in exotic Mayan locations to save his loved one from the evil industrialist before he achieves his ultimate goal of becoming a Mayan God. The story is rife with mentions of Mayan culture and their gods.
You get the use of a weird scythe-like weapon which has three other versions of itself as well as four elemental powers you can use to devastate numerous enemies. The different variations allow you to attack in different ways and with different spells. One is a mace-like weapon that's slower but hits harder. Another is a scythe for faster if weaker attacks and so on. The hack and slash elements are well done and flashy, if standard. You recover health and mana via other death masks items found in the level as well as off fallen enemies. The only hidden items in this game are XP masks and they aren't too hard to find.
Marlow Briggs has a fairly lacking options menu. Game will only display in 16:9 resolutions (with 50, 59, 60Hz options for some resolutions). It’s letterboxed or cropped depending on the differing aspect ratios. AA, V-Sync, Field of View and anisotropic filtering can’t be changed. The AA used seems to be FXAA according to
. Keys can be rebound if needed though I suggest running this game with a controller. You should be fine without one but spectacle fighters tend to play better with a controller. Audio sliders include: effects, music, dialog and master volume. Can’t go wrong with those choices.
Graphics are a modern day realistic style. It's ok but a bit low-fidelity. Soundtrack is an over the top orchestral collection of tracks with big bombastic choirs singing. There is one thing I should note. Many of the “cutscenes” are a collection of still images of Briggs in a, for lack of a better term, badass pose. Whether its slicing enemies apart or leaping over a boulder, it doesn't matter. Sort of like a very fancy 3D slideshow. I still can’t tell if the devs were saving money, being artsy or confident in their graphics team. It’s a little weird when you're playing the game but I guess it works. Oh one final note, there are challenge modes but I didn't really bother with them.
Summed up, Marlow Briggs and the Mask of Death is an average game that somehow kept me entertained the entire time. I think the combination of over the top action, voice acting and a care-free attitude in the developers is why. The pace is just about right too. This isn't game-of-the-year material, it’s not the best of the genre and its not a unforgettable experience but Marlow isn't trying to waste your time either. Each level doesn't outstay its welcome and the combat remains challenging without getting too aggravating. Characters are fairly well fleshed out too and you get some reason to care about them. So, consider picking it up if you need a new spectacle fighter.

Sometimes, a game comes along that asks little of you. Instead of pretension and criminal seriousness, there is an earnestness and a willingness to have fun with itself - even when its technical trappings are rough around the edges. With obvious inspiration being taken from the flashy beat-em-ups a la Bayonetta and Devil May Cry, Marlow Briggs' action is completely relentless, with the story travelling along at the same pace. While it is not the prettiest game out there, its visuals are stylized such that one can't help but be overwhelmed by the sheer amount of preposterous explosions.
It doesn't push the envelope in terms of mechanics, story, or social commentary, but it does have exploding red barrels and a scythe. What more could one possibly need for a $5 purchase such as this?

It's "God of War" meets a somewhat cheesy "B-movie" with some good humor sprinkled into the mix. The gameplay is a mix of platforming, "arena" hack-n-slash, with some minigame-esque challenges dotted throughout.
The gameplay is pretty much button-mashing for the majority of the time, with the occasional timing challenge thrown in (such as boss fights) so it doesn't require much effort. The characters aren't really "storied" but they have a lot of personality. The banter in the game is quite enjoyable, with the "Mask of Death" having some great moments with Marlow.
Overall, don't take the game seriously, save it for an evening that you just want to have some brainless fun, and play. It's quite enjoyable, and considering the price during sales drops to less than $1, you can't get a better deal. It's a bargain-bin find that is superisingly good.

In Dark and Bright you play Gourchweasel and his friends and you help them to find out more about that weird world they're travelling through. The game combines some RPG elements with arcade or puzzle elements, but all in all it is a story-driven game with a focus on what's happening to the four friends in that abstract world.
And that's what I like about the game the most - the story is good! Really. I enjoyed it a lot, also a lot more than in some other, bigger and well-known RPGs. The game does a great job in telling the player the right amount of information (or only vague hints in the beginning) so that I was always interested in how the story continues. It all starts with a mysterious cutscene about two unknown characters at a bonfire - then we're following Grouchweasel on his journey. And that journey is weird, confusing, but interesting and also thrilling at the same time. There are many things that made me enjoy it so much - things happening again with small changes to the dialogues, the memories becoming more and more intense as you progress, mysterious characters who sometimes totally confuse you, the whole tone to everything with these simple but weird graphics which fit well to the overall atmosphere. I can't write more about that without spoilers. Maybe this story will also make you think a little bit about your own life, which I find amazing. So, if you're a fan of good stories in RPGs - this might be the right game for you!
The gameplay experience I've had was okay, but nothing spectacular. You need to accomplish several levels to progress with the story. The levels were okay, some were awesome like the disco because of the music and the whole feeling, others were more mediocre I think. The more levels you accomplish, the more and more challenging they become. However, the difficulty was just perfect for me when I played on Normal or sometimes even Challenging. I can't really recommend Difficult, it was too hard and resulted in a permanent death for me, kind of xD
I think after you get used to the characters' special skills, you can have a nice time playing the game. I enjoyed improving their skills and levitating or being invisible for a long time. But I really needed to get used to it. Sometimes I just forgot that a particular skill could have helped me a lot in several situations, which I found out only later.
Also, I just kept forgetting that I unlocked some of the bonus levels. You just tend to forget that after completing a task for an NPC, you need to return to them so that they unlock something for you. I think the interface could be improved here, or at least the player should be reminded or anything.
There is also optional content like a Colosseum where you can fight a lot, or some extra levels which are highly difficult.
All in all, I've had a good experience playing the game and I can definitely recommend it! The story was thrilling and the characters were loveable! There are some RPG Maker games with very good stories out there and I'd say this one is one of them.
The gameplay was okay, but not as exciting as the story.

Let me just start by saying that this is an okay game, but I struggle to say that it is a very good one. I have only played the game for about three and a half hours for reasons I will go into in a moment. Let me start by addressing the cons and move on to the pros afterward. I use a Playstation controller so I will go over controls as follows:
Cons:
-The combat system is very basic. You have one combo for each character via square, but each character has one special move with triangle. There is a far range attack with square and triangle can sometimes do more than one thing, but not always. You have a guard button with circle and can jump with x. You can do air attacks with square and sometimes triangle depending on the character. You have a guard break and a throw type move. Your R1 gives you the power to avoid moves if you are a logia user such as Ace using your top bar, and does other things generally involving powering you up for other characters such as Whitebeard. L1 is probably the strongest mechanic as it gives you three special moves per character, though sometimes these are not always very viable special moves. You also have a sort of awakening full power mode which does take a bit to build up and gives you the ability to do a special move at the end. Usually this mode only really makes you a little stronger, but for some characters like Luffy it does change your moveset. Overall, combat is not the strongest and you'll find most characters play somewhat similarly and may get a little bored of it.
-The story is EXTREMELY short. You play only one part of the One Piece story, the one where you try to save Ace from Execution. This consists of you playing four different characters primarily, Luffy, Whitebeard, Ace, and Akainu. You will occasionally play as other characters via side missions or have them in your team to switch between. Some of the missions, usually side missions, are particularly extremely hard compared to others, but this isn't the biggest deal and can be overcome given a few tries. Quite frankly, that actually adds to the experience because of how short the overall story is. Each character outside of Ace has around 10 battles or so. It also happens to repeat itself as you play different characters, you'll probably see the same scene with Ace towards the end about three times or so total, as that is in multiple stories. You can skip scenes, but it's still annoying. The format of the story is probably the issue here, because if they had just spread out their 30-40 missions through different One Piece story arcs, it may have added much more to the experience.
-You have to gain Beli to unlock characters, and while this isn't the worst mechanic I've seen in a game for gaining new characters, it can be annoying, as by the end of the story you will most likely only be able to afford 5-10 characters to play as depending on how your experience goes, not including supports which must also be purchased with Beli.
-Some characters are very annoying to fight against, such as Buggy, as they have the ability to spam extremely strong and annoying moves at you which lock you in place with no method of escape until it's done.
-The support system isn't something I am a big fan of as they don't do a great job of explaining each character's powers and they are, for the most part, just passive bonuses to your fighter.
-You take and do a lot of damage, meaning battles really don't last as long as you might like. Yes, you can form teams of up to 9 people depending on the mode, but it seems like each character should have the ability to survive more hits rather than having to switch out constantly due to your character dying so fast.
Pros:
-The game is an entertaining One Piece experience if you don't mind the above cons. The combat system isn't fantastic but it also isn't horrible or boring per say, it's just a little repetetive. It's also quite fun to play as certain characters such as Aokoji who I found to be especially enjoyable due to his technical nature.
-There are more than 40 characters to my knowledge that, despite taking a while to collect, are all unique in some way. The combat system is very similar no matter who you play, but each character does have individual abilities to try out.
-As an anime gaming experience, it's certainly not the worst, nor is it the worst fighting game, it does have fun merits especially knowing you're playing as the One Piece crew.
Overall, I'd probably give this game a 5/10. If you get it on sale, it can be a 6/10, but it simply doesn't hold up to the $40 asking price. If the story was more spread out and a little longer, and the combat system was a little less simple, I could certainly see this being a 7/10 or even 8/10, but as it stands I don't think it is quite that good. Still, I'd recommend this to any One Piece fan as long as they get it on a sale of some kind.

First off, i want to respond to someone that clearly hasn't played the game long enough to know the basic combat mechanics, so people won't avoid this game based on a rather misinformed review:

"-can't tank them"
You can. Maximize vigor, strength, and put on a heavy armor.
...But that still doesn't mean you should, since dead character will stay dead. Avoid any direct confrontation if possible, whether it's against looters or zombies.
"-can't kite them"
Every type of enemy has a certain vision range. Just make your party hides in a certain spot and *very* carefully send one party member to kite one or two of the zombies.
"-can't evade them"
Put more points towards agility. But this is a survival strategy game in the first place, so what you really want to do is to kill off any threats as carefully and quietly as possible.
And to add: positioning is *crucial* in any strategy game, so if you somehow messed up and got a party member surrounded by zombies, then you're the only one to blame for that.
"-can't sneak past them"
Stealth is a totally viable option, and is the preferred way of doing things in this game. Zombies has a rather small(er) visibility cone, so you CAN evade them and quite easily too compared to sneaking past looters.
They do have better sense of hearing though, so if you're planning to do a sneak attack do it quickly. Initiate the attack a few squares away from behind the zombie.
"-must rely on luck to beat them"
Every strategy game that has RNG relies on both skill and luck. I see no problem with this.
"-if you don't outnumber them 2 or 3 to 1, it has a high probability of a loss."
Outnumbering them does indeed kills them more effectively, but that doesn't mean you can't send a party member with high Vigor and Strength/Agility plus a high enough melee skill to face off against a zombie one-on-one.
I'm not saying the game is perfect. It's buggy at times, writing is... okay, and the graphics and animations are not exactly what you'd call stellar...
But the game still offers exploration in a rather big world map, the strategy part is quite solid, you can recruit and manage survivors who also gives you choices and consequences that matters, and the best aspect i personally love the most: homebase management. I just wish they would offer more base other than the school though, and more interations between each survivors.
Overall it's at least a 7/10 game, and is totally worth the price tag.

(Note: I fully completed this game on the Wii U, so I have the experience to write a review)
Shantae and the Pirate's Curse is a 2D Metroidvania Style Platformer with a little bit of RPG sprinkled in. The game takes place after Risky's Revenge. There's a spirit of a once evil pirate called the Pirate Master. His spirit awakens to find out he's capable of taking over Sequin Land, and tries to spread the area with Dark Magic, effectively ruling it slowly but surely. It's up to Shantae, paired up with Risky Boots, to stop the Pirate Master by going to multiple islands and taking out the areas where he's getting his power.
This game is SO much better than Risky's Revenge ever hopes to be. It has a much faster pace overall, so it never feels sluggish. Shantae's attack, movement speed, and even the gameplay itself is generally quick, making killing enemies much less slow and tedious, and making the game overall a better, more paced experience. Other than that, it also has a much more interesting story with tons of character dialog and more immersive character development with funny and witty humor.
You aren't limited to one huge area like in Risky's Revenge, but you now have multiple islands to explore, each with their own individual theme and secrets to uncover; also their own dungeon. It certainly brings a breath of fresh air very often with each of the island's own unique style of puzzles, platforming, and fights. Pretty much makes the game itself very diverse so nothing is boring.
Shantae can no longer dance, but find some of Risky's pirate gear so she is granted more abilites. For example, she can find Risky's hat to have herself gently float downwards or use wind to go up, or Risky's pistol to solve puzzles and shoot enemies from afar. You'll find a new item in each dungeon, and they are well worth the journey to get them. Of course, it also makes the puzzles much more varied
The game is a little more on the RPG side this time around. Shantae's hair and Risky's weapons can be upgraded, and Shantae can even learn some new moves. It takes lots of money to get everything fully upgraded, so spend your gems wisely. It doesn't sound like much, but it's actually alot to upgrade. There's also healing items that enemies drop, and sometimes even attack items. You can access all of that by simply going to the item menu and using it, easy peasy.
Overall, this game is wonderful, and a FANTASTIC step up from Risky's Revenge. If you can get this, get it. It's a wonderful platformer series that has a great, memorable story, and fun, fast gameplay.

Risky's Revenge review:
This game is good, and should be bought.

- Funny and unique dialouge.
- Wonderful sprite animation
- Awesome soundtrack
- High replay value (After beating the steam version 3 different times I will have beaten this 10 times)
Cons:
- Bad for players who do not have a thrill for adventure. This game does not exactly tell you what you have to do and where to do it. You have to use your brain and the tiny amount of hints the game gives to find out where things are. This is however good cause what's an adventure platformer if the game just tells you what to do and how to do it.
- Grinding Gems to get items. The items for upgrades and moves can be way too expensive and useless. Like I said I beat this game a lot of times, I never used the back kick move, or the back dash. Back dash being 100 gems (not bad) and the back kick being 400 which is too much for something I never had to use. Also you have to upgrade your hair strength, whip speed, scimitar, and pistol 3 times which adds up to a lot of gems. It's not that bad to grind for them but it could of been done better.
So if you like Metroid/Castlevenia you will love this game. The story in this one is more deep than Risky's Revenge and the original GBC game. It is totally worth the 20 dollars to get.
That concludes this review with the 2 minor cons (one being really minor), I still have to give this game a wonderful score.

Steam Marines is a contained, lovingly crafted tactical squad-based roguelike. It does have some issues. The random level generation is desperate, creating rooms with too many doors almost as often as it creates rooms with no doors at all. Enemy placement is similarly unpredictable, and yet the AI is predictable. This is a flawed game, but enjoyable, and if the challenge isn't always fair, well, at least it is there.

I just immediately got annoyed by the lack of ability to play at 1920x1080 at full screen (choosing one or the other is fine, but when I select both the bottom part of the game gets cut off so all I can see are the top 2 out of the 6 total options on the main menu).

Bottom Line: A contrived attemp at a turn-based rogue-like squad combat sci-fi RPG that has a painfully slow start and so many key bindings that you may need to actually forget some general knowledge to make room in your brain for them (Oh and the tutorial basically only tells you how to move and shoot). I do not recommend this game to individuals with short attention spans (you know who you are) as you will likely not get past the tutorial. I also don't recommend the game to people in search of another good Rogue-like (the reason I bought it...), this game is not it.
The Long of it (4 paragraphs):
I'm gonna be honest, I tried to get into this game. Really and truly. After roughly five separate attempts over the past year I finally gave up. I know I only have a little less than an hour of play time on it, and truthfully I didn't get far past the tutorial on any of my attempted plays; but what I saw from the time I spent on the game I could tell the game had a serious flaw: even after the tutorial, there is a strong chance you still won't be able to play the game effectively. Now, I don't mind teaching myself how to play a game, but as far as I'm concerned any rogue-like game that I can't get comfortable playing within the first 15 minutes should reconsider its place in the genre.
Expanding on the utter lack of a real tutorial: The tutorial informs you of critical game mechanics...... that's it. At the start of the game you learn how to move, shoot, reload, and open doors/chests. It completely glosses over the 40+ controls/key bindings as well as basically neglecting to explain most of the UI, which is, by the way, and utter trainwreck.
Looking past the lack of initial information, the level design is not well though out. At all. Most rooms are too small to have more than two of your squad comfortably occupy (since they are likely also completely filled with enemies). Sometimes you will start on a level in a room filled with enemies, sometimes the room doesn't have an exit, sometimes filled with enemies and also no exit. The 'rogue-likeness' of this game is sloppy at best and provides a purely annoying game environment, as opposed to that fresh feeling you get from ideally executed rogue-likes. It almost seems like the devs wanted to make a game that spanned as many genres as possible so they put in a crappy random number generator and called it a rogue-like.
Suffice to say, this game is like Indian food, it tries very hard to be a lot of things, and looks enticing, but often leaves a bad taste in your mouth. After you play what you thought was supposed to be a turn-based squad combat, rogue-like sci-fi RPG, you realize that there is just too much going on and you were silly to think it would deliver everything you thought it would.

I'm not entirely sure whether I should recommend this game or not, as I have rather mixed feelings about it.

-nice punch of different items, both interesting and useful,
-good range of enemies (considering the length), and so on.
-It has funny odd things, like a collectable painting that can be used for random effect.

-It has terrible graphics: sometimes I'm not sure what I'm looking at, while occasionally I have difficulties with reading the text. Sometimes its very hard to say whether a piece of wall is bashed or if it's semi-destroyed. In some maps, the wall tiles are so dark that I have to look the screen from different angle (benefits of flat screen) to be able to actually differ them from background or unexplored tiles. Some enemies can't be recognized from each others, until they blow on your face.
-Moving around often bugs like hell: unit graphic may stay behind from actual position during moving, sometimes the whole movement is ignored. I have had two marines standing in a same tile more than once. Luckily this mainly plagues PCs, it could easily make the game unplayable if this would affect NPCs as well.
-Shop pricing skyrockets like stockmarket-bubble.
-Item prices increases every time you enter a shop.
-Shop offers four items, chosen randomly. Combined with above, trying to buy a med-kit can become very, very expensive.
-You can't sell items.
-Using mouse over the battlefield is buggy, and supposed benefits are often broken. Not to forget that sometimes moving the mouse on the map area causes heavy lagging and shooting CPU-load to roof.
-Occasionally "targeting indicator" does not appear as supposed to, you have to rotate the character or switch between characters for it to show.
-Game is balanced in a wrong way: You must make sure that you wont be shot at all, because enemies will tear apart your marines too easily, even on easy-difficulty. This means that you must use lure-tactics constantly, and even a single mistake may result to complete failure.

Heard about the game via the PewDiePie thing and decided to check it out.
The first bit setting up your backstory was pretty well done and the twists were gripping.  To be honest most of the dialog in the game is an example of awesome writing.
The story is fairly decent, after suffering a personal tragedy you sign up as a forest lookout for the summer.  You spend the next two and a half months building up a relationship with another lookout who you report to (your supervisor).  During that time the events craft a series of strange events that culminate in a shocking discovery during a time when the entire area is in danger of being engulfed in a massive fire.
I found the story pretty gripping.  I had intended to just check it out but ended up playing until I completed the game.  This game is fairly short but about the normal length for this type of adventure genre game (most average 2 to 5 hours, this one was about 3 and a half and I missed two achievements from not completely exploring and one for not picking up "Shelly" Duval).
I will say again, this is an adventure game in the vien of a point-and-click mystery but within a 3D game space and more immersive game mechanics.  The mechanics are pretty solid, at no point did I find it hard to get around in the game due to the mechianics specifically though walking up to ropes to rappel down did get annoying after a while as there is a very small alignment window.
There are plenty of places to explore and a lot of them have correcponding dialog which is cool.  It helps make it feel as through you are not just being railed through an area of the game and gives you a reason to explore a bit.  There were very few places where there were not any dialog options that were not a part of the game/suspense.
On replayability I don't have anything as I have not tried yet to see if different choices lead to a different outcome in the backstory of your character.  There is an option to play it with audio commentary from the developers so I make check that out later.  That said, similar games to this normally don't have a lot of replayability.
Overall I find this to be a solid game and if you like adventure games it is a pretty sure bet you will get into this quickly.
I would give it a 7/10.
